questions.domain: ML Model Development

options.text: Increase the number of epochs.
Increase the number of neurons in the hidden layers.
Increase the number of layers.
Increase the number of instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism distributes training work across GPUs and instances. Increasing the number of instances increases the training cluster size and available parallel compute capacity, which can reduce wall-clock training time. More epochs or a larger/deeper network instead increase the amount of training computation.

**Learn more:** [Scaling training - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/distributed-training-scenarios.html) · [Introduction to the SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-parallel-intro.html)

A company has trained an ML model that is packaged in a container. The company will integrate this model with an existing Python web application. The company needs to host the model on AWS using Kubernetes.  
  
The company does not want to manage the control plane and must provision resources repeatably. The infrastructure must be provisioned using Python.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation to provision Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Set up a Kubernetes cluster. Host the model container on the Kubernetes cluster.

Use the AWS CLI to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.

Use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.

Use AWS CloudFormation to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS provides a managed Kubernetes control plane, so the company does not operate that control-plane infrastructure. AWS CDK supports defining EKS infrastructure in Python, providing repeatable infrastructure-as-code deployment; the container image can be stored in Amazon ECR and run as a workload on EKS.

**Learn more:** [EKS Control Plane](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/control-plane.html) · [AWS CDK Python EKS Cluster construct](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/api/v2/python/aws_cdk.aws_eks/Cluster.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use Amazon SageMaker to produce image-based classification ratings. The company has 6 ТВ of training data stored on an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP storage virtual machine (SVM). The SVM is in the same VPC as SageMaker.  
  
An ML engineer must make the training data available to ML models in the SageMaker environment.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Mount the FSx for ONTAP file system as a volume to the SageMaker Instance.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to link the S3 bucket to the FSx for ONTAP file system.
Create a catalog connection from SageMaker Data Wrangler to the FSx for ONTAP file system.
Create a direct connection from SageMaker Data Wrangler to the FSx for ONTAP file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP SVMs provide NFS endpoints for data access. Mounting the ONTAP file system on a SageMaker instance in the same VPC gives the ML environment direct access to the existing training files without copying the 6 ТВ dataset or using an unsupported Data Wrangler connection type.

**Learn more:** [Accessing your FSx for ONTAP data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html) · [Mounting volumes on Linux clients](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/attach-linux-client.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is developing a logistic regression model to predict customer churn for subscription services. The ML engineer is using a dataset that includes two string variables: `location` and `job_seniority_level`. The `location` variable has 3 distinct values, while the `job_seniority_level` variable has more than 10 distinct values.  
  
The ML engineer must preprocess these variables.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Apply tokenization to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level.
Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level
Apply binning to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.
Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.

questions.explanation:
One-hot encoding is appropriate for `location` because its categories are nominal and should not be assigned an artificial order. Ordinal encoding is appropriate for `job_seniority_level` because seniority levels have an inherent order. Categorical string values must be converted to numeric representations for use as logistic-regression features; standard scaling and binning are not categorical encoders.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to build several ML prediction models. Its training data is stored in Amazon S3. The complete dataset is more than 5 ТВ in size and contains CSV, JSON, Apache Parquet, and simple text files.  
  
The data must be processed through several consecutive steps. These steps include complex manipulations that can require hours to complete. Some processing includes natural language processing (NLP) transformations. The entire process must be automated.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Process data at each step by using Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Automate the process by using Data Wrangler jobs.
Use Amazon SageMaker notebooks for each data processing step. Automate the process by using Amazon EventBridge.
Process data at each step by using AWS Lambda functions. Automate the process by using AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge.
Use Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to create a pipeline of data processing steps. Automate the pipeline by using Amazon EventBridge.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines orchestrates interconnected, dependency-based ML workflow steps and can include SageMaker processing jobs for large-scale, long-running custom data transformations such as NLP. Amazon EventBridge can automatically initiate a pipeline execution, including in response to events such as new objects in an S3 bucket. AWS Lambda is unsuitable for transformations that run for hours because a Lambda invocation has a maximum execution time of 15 minutes.

**Learn more:** [Pipelines overview - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines-overview.html) · [Schedule Pipeline Runs - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipeline-eventbridge.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to reduce the time required for the training job."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will satisfy this requirement?"}],"
",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Increase the number of epochs.","B":"Increase the number of neurons in the hidden layers.","C":"Increase the number of layers.","D":"Increase the number of instances."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"Amazon SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism distributes training work across GPUs and instances. ",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Process data at each step by using Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Automate the process by using Data Wrangler jobs.","B":"Use Amazon SageMaker notebooks for each data processing step. Automate the process by using Amazon EventBridge.","C":"Process data at each step by using AWS Lambda functions. Automate the process by using AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge.","D":"Use Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to create a pipeline of data processing steps. Automate the pipeline by using Amazon EventBridge."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"Amazon SageMaker Pipelines orchestrates interconnected, dependency-based ML workflow steps and can include SageMaker processing jobs for large-scale, long-running custom data transformations such as NLP. Amazon EventBridge can automatically initiate a pipeline execution, including in response to events such as new objects in an S3 bucket. AWS Lambda is unsuitable for transformations that run for hours because a Lambda invocation has a maximum execution time of 15 minutes.

**Learn more:** [Pipelines overview - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines-overview.html) · [Schedule Pipeline Runs - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipeline-eventbridge.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"859088f7-3afa-4616-a3b6-54a203cf4fce","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-machine-learning-engineer-associate-mla-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
An ML engineer must implement a solution to host a trained ML model. The request rate for the model will vary throughout the day.  
  
The ML engineer needs a scalable solution that minimizes costs while the model is not being used. The solution must also retain the model capacity to respond to requests during periods of peak use.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create AWS Lambda functions that have fixed concurrency to host the model. Configure the Lambda functions to automatically scale based on the number of requests to the model.
Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses AWS Fargate. Set a static number of tasks to handle requests during times of peak usage.

Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. Deploy multiple copies of the model to the endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer to route traffic between the different copies of the model at the endpoint.
Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. Create SageMaker endpoint auto scaling policies that are based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics to adjust the number of instances dynamically.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker endpoint auto scaling uses Amazon CloudWatch metrics to dynamically adjust the number of endpoint instances. It scales out as workload demand rises to provide peak capacity and scales in when demand falls, eliminating unnecessary provisioned-instance cost.

**Learn more:** [Automatic scaling of Amazon SageMaker AI models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling.html) · [Auto scaling policy overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-policy.html)

A company uses an Amazon Redshift database as its sole data source. Some of its data is sensitive.  
  
A data scientist needs to use some sensitive data from the database. An ML engineer must provide the data scientist access without transforming the source data or storing anonymized data in the database.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Configure dynamic data masking policies to control how sensitive data is shared with the data scientist at query time.
Create a materialized view with masking logic on top of the database. Grant the necessary read permissions to the data scientist.
Unload the Amazon Redshift data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create schema-on-read with masking logic. Share the view with the data scientist.
Unload the Amazon Redshift data to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue job to anonymize the data. Share the dataset with the data scientist.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Redshift dynamic data masking applies role- or user-specific obfuscation when sensitive columns are queried, without modifying the underlying database data. It directly provides controlled access to sensitive values without creating or storing an anonymized copy, and avoids the added work of materialized views, S3 exports, Athena, or AWS Glue.

**Learn more:** [Dynamic data masking - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/t_ddm.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is importing a custom model from the Hugging Face Hub into Amazon Bedrock. The ML engineer wants to use the model through the Amazon Bedrock API in an agentic AI application.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Import the model for deployment by using Amazon Bedrock On-Demand mode.
Convert the model to a quantized format. Import the quantized model after conversion.
Import the model directly by using the Amazon SageMaker AI SDK in the agentic AI application.
During the model import process, configure an auto-scaling policy before using the model in the agentic AI application.
In the import job, provide the complete Amazon S3 URI that points to the Hugging Face model files. Ensure that the S3 URI is in the same AWS account as the Amazon Bedrock import job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import uses a model import job whose source is an Amazon S3 URI containing model files in Hugging Face weights format. After import, the model can be invoked through Amazon Bedrock APIs with on-demand throughput, which provides the API-based inference required by an agentic application. Quantizing the model and configuring an auto-scaling policy are not required import steps.

**Learn more:** [Use Custom model import to import a customized open-source model into Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-import-model.html) · [Submit a model import job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-import-model-job.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A hospital uses an ML model to validate x-ray results and runs a nightly batch-inference job. The hospital must generate a daily report on model data quality and model performance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Schedule a monitoring job in Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor. Generate the monitoring results for the model and data.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that includes the metrics for processing steps in the nightly batch inference job. Compare the baseline resource metrics. Share the dashboard link.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a custom recipe job that uses the Numerical Statistics data quality check for the model file. Generate the results.
Create a SageMaker AI pipeline that includes a QualityCheck step to run monitoring jobs. Generate the monitoring results for the model and the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor can run recurring monitoring schedules for batch transform workloads, compare captured inference inputs and outputs with baseline statistics and constraints, and generate monitoring reports. It supports data-quality monitoring and model-quality metrics such as accuracy; model-quality measurement requires matching ground-truth labels for the predictions.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Schedule monitoring jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-scheduling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare company uses an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint to host a model that predicts patient readmission risk for hospitals. The company wants to predict patient readmissions with high accuracy and is willing to accept false positives. The current model’s performance has declined over the past year.  
  
The company trains and deploys a new model as a shadow variant to test it on live traffic from hospitals. The company monitors the new model’s performance for one month. During that testing month, the shadow variant has higher recall than the existing model but lower precision.  
  
What should the company do next?

options.text: Promote the shadow variant to full production.
Extend the shadow testing period to capture more data. Monitor the new model to determine whether precision improves.
Use a blue/green deployment strategy to allocate a small percentage of traffic to the shadow variant to reduce model errors.
Disable the shadow variant and roll back to the main variant.

questions.explanation:
Recall measures how many actual patient readmissions the model identifies. Since detecting readmissions is the priority and false positives are acceptable, the higher-recall shadow model better satisfies the operating requirement despite its lower precision. SageMaker AI shadow testing compares a shadow variant with production traffic without returning shadow responses to callers; after satisfactory evaluation, the shadow variant can be promoted to production.

**Learn more:** [Create a shadow test - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests-create.html) · [Validation of models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-validation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an existing Amazon SageMaker model (v1) on a production endpoint. The company develops a new model version (v2) and must test v2 in production before replacing v1 with v2.  
  
The company must implement a solution that minimizes the risk of v2 producing incorrect output in production. The solution must prevent any disruption to production traffic while changing to v2.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a second production variant for v2. Assign 1% of the traffic to v2 and 99% of the traffic to v1. Collect all the output of v2 in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, switch all the traffic to v2.

Create a second production variant for v2. Assign 10% of the traffic to v2 and 90% of the traffic to v1. Collect all the output of v2 in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, switch all the traffic to v2.

Deploy v2 to a new endpoint. Turn on data capturing for the production endpoint. Write a script to pass 100% of input data to v2. If v2 performs as expected, deactivate the v1 endpoint and direct the traffic to v2.
Deploy v2 into a shadow variant that samples 100% of the inference requests. Collect all the output in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, promote v2 to production.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon SageMaker shadow variant receives replicated live inference requests, but its responses are not returned to callers; v1 continues to receive and respond to production traffic. Sampling 100% of requests lets v2 be assessed against the full production workload, and the logged outputs can be evaluated before promoting v2 to the production variant.

**Learn more:** [Validation of models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-validation.html) · [Create a shadow test - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests-create.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must ensure that a dataset complies with regulations concerning personally identifiable information (PII). The ML engineer will use the data to train an ML model on Amazon SageMaker instances. SageMaker must not use any PII.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Use the Amazon Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API call to redact the PII from the data. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Access the S3 bucket from the SageMaker instances for model training.

Use the Amazon Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API call to redact the PII from the data. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system to the SageMaker instances for model training.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to cleanse the dataset of PII. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system to the SageMaker instances for model training.
Use Amazon Macie for automatic discovery of PII in the data. Remove the PII. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the SageMaker instances for model training.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend can identify PII and produce redacted text, while Amazon S3 is a directly supported data source for SageMaker training jobs. Storing the sanitized dataset in S3 lets SageMaker train only on the redacted copy without the additional VPC connectivity and file-system management required for Amazon EFS. Amazon Macie discovers and reports sensitive data; it does not itself remove PII.

**Learn more:** [Detecting PII entities - Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/how-pii.html) · [Setting up training jobs to access datasets - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-access-training-data.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs ML models on premises using custom Python scripts and proprietary datasets. The company uses PyTorch. Building the models requires unique domain knowledge. The company needs to migrate the models to AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Use SageMaker built-in algorithms to train the proprietary datasets.
Use SageMaker script mode and premade images for ML frameworks.
Build a container on AWS that includes custom packages and a choice of ML frameworks.
Purchase similar production models through AWS Marketplace.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer uses Amazon SageMaker AI to train a deep learning model. During testing, the model exhibits high variance. The ML engineer must adjust a hyperparameter to improve generalization without significantly increasing training time.  
  
Which solution will **MOST** improve model generalization?

options.text: Increase the number of layers in the neural network.
Reduce the learning rate of the optimizer.
Increase the L2 regularization parameter
Increase the batch size significantly.

questions.explanation:
High variance is characteristic of overfitting. Increasing L2 regularization penalizes large model weights, constraining model complexity and reducing overfitting, thereby improving performance on unseen data. AWS documentation identifies increasing regularization as an adjustment for overfitting and describes L2 regularization as reducing overall weight values.

**Learn more:** [Example: Viewing a Training and Validation Curve - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-valid-curve.html) · [IP Insights Hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/ip-insights-hyperparameters.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an internal cost-estimation tool that uses an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. Users upload high-resolution images to the tool.  
  
The model must process every image and predict the cost of the object shown in the image. The model must also notify the user when processing has finished.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use batch transform jobs for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to notify users.

Store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use an asynchronous inference strategy for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify users.

Store the images in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use batch transform jobs for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to notify users.

Store the images in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use an asynchronous inference strategy for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify users.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI Asynchronous Inference uses Amazon S3 for request payloads and processes inference requests asynchronously. Its endpoint configuration can specify Amazon SNS success and error topics, allowing users to be notified when processing completes.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use Amazon SageMaker to host an ML model that runs on CPU and provides real-time predictions. The model will receive intermittent traffic during business hours and no traffic during some periods after business hours. The company requires the most cost-effective way to serve inference requests.  
  
Which hosting option meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Add a schedule-based auto scaling policy to handle traffic surges during business hours.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint. Configure increased provisioned concurrency during business hours.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint. Configure an auto scaling policy that scales in to zero outside business hours.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that activates the endpoint during business hours only.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference is suited to synchronous workloads with intermittent traffic: it automatically scales with demand and scales to zero when no requests arrive, avoiding charges for idle compute. Provisioned concurrency can be scheduled higher during predictable business-hour demand to keep the endpoint warm and reduce cold starts.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html) · [Automatically scale Provisioned Concurrency for a serverless endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints-autoscale.html)

options.text: Configure a blue/green deployment with all-at-once traffic shifting.
Configure a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting and a size of 10%.
Configure a shadow test with a traffic sampling percentage of 10%.
Configure a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size of 1.

questions.explanation:
A SageMaker rolling deployment updates an endpoint fleet in batches. With a rolling batch size of 1, it provisions one instance for the new model, shifts traffic while the remaining old-model instances continue serving, and then terminates one old instance before the next batch. This requires only one instance of additional capacity during the update and preserves endpoint availability. Blue/green deployments instead provision a full new fleet.

**Learn more:** [Use rolling deployments - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deployment-guardrails-rolling.html) · [RollingUpdatePolicy - Amazon SageMaker](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_RollingUpdatePolicy.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has AWS Glue data-processing jobs orchestrated through an AWS Glue workflow. The AWS Glue jobs can run on a schedule or be started manually.  
  
The company is developing Amazon SageMaker Pipelines for ML model development. During the data-processing phase of model development, the pipelines will use output from the AWS Glue jobs. An ML engineer must implement a solution that integrates the AWS Glue jobs with the pipelines.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions for orchestration of the pipelines and the AWS Glue jobs.
Use processing steps in SageMaker Pipelines. Configure inputs that point to the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the AWS Glue jobs.
Use Callback steps in SageMaker Pipelines to start the AWS Glue workflow and to stop the pipelines until the AWS Glue jobs finish running.
Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the pipelines and the AWS Glue jobs in the desired order.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines Callback steps support integration with processes and AWS services that Pipelines does not directly provide. A callback step sends work to a customer-specified handler and waits for that handler to report step success or failure, allowing the handler to start the AWS Glue workflow and resume the pipeline only after the Glue jobs complete.

**Learn more:** [Add a step - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/build-and-manage-steps-types.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A bank must use Amazon SageMaker AI to build an ML model that identifies which customers qualify for a new product. The bank must use algorithms directly supported by SageMaker AI. The model must be explainable to the bank’s regulators.  
  
Which modeling approach satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Train the model by using the Object2Vec algorithm.
Train the model by using the linear learner algorithm.
Train a neural network.
Train the model by using the k-means algorithm.

questions.explanation:
Linear Learner is a SageMaker AI built-in supervised algorithm for classification and regression. For customer eligibility, it can perform binary classification using a linear decision function; its feature coefficients and classification threshold make the basis of predictions comparatively transparent for regulatory review. SageMaker AI also provides model-explainability tooling for auditing and regulatory requirements.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a custom extract, transform, and load (ETL) process on premises. The ETL process is written in the R language and runs for an average of 6 hours. The company wants to migrate this process to run on AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function created from a container image to run the ETL jobs.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI processing jobs with a custom Docker image stored in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR).
Use Amazon SageMaker AI script mode to build a Docker image. Run the ETL jobs by using SageMaker Notebook Jobs.

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor network metrics and CPU metrics for resource optimization during model training.
Create AWS Glue DataBrew recipes to correct the data based on statistics from the model output.
Use SageMaker Clarify to evaluate the model and training data for underlying patterns that might affect accuracy.

A company is preparing data to train a new ML model on Amazon SageMaker AI. The data has not previously been used for ML training and includes duplicates and some missing values.  
  
The company needs to improve data quality and identify any statistical bias in the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor can create a data-quality baseline from a dataset, generating descriptive statistics and suggested feature constraints that serve as data-quality rules. Amazon SageMaker Clarify computes pre-training bias metrics on raw training datasets to identify statistical bias before model training.

questions.question:
An ML engineer must use an ML model to predict apartment prices in a particular location.  
  
Which metric should the ML engineer use to assess the model's performance?

options.text: Accuracy
Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
F1 score
Mean absolute error (MAE)

questions.explanation:
Apartment-price prediction is a regression problem with a continuous numeric output. Mean absolute error (MAE) measures the average absolute difference between actual and predicted values; lower MAE indicates more accurate predictions. Accuracy, AUC, and F1 score evaluate classification performance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Introduction to tabular data | Vertex AI | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/tabular-data/tabular101)

questions.question:
An ML engineer must use an ML model to predict apartment prices in a particular location.  
  
Which metric should the ML engineer use to assess the model's performance?

options.text: Use SageMaker AI IAM roles and policies to control access. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for encryption.
Use AWS PrivateLink for SageMaker AI to control access. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for encryption.
Use AWS PrivateLink for SageMaker AI to control access. Use VPC only mode for encryption.
Use SageMaker AI IAM roles and policies to control access. Use AWS CloudTrail for encryption.

questions.explanation:
AWS KMS customer managed keys let the company control key policies and permissions for encryption and decryption. SageMaker AI IAM roles and policies can limit access to the facial data and SageMaker resources to authorized employees. AWS PrivateLink controls network connectivity, VPC-only mode does not provide encryption, and AWS CloudTrail records activity rather than encrypting data.

**Learn more:** [Protect Data at Rest Using Encryption - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/encryption-at-rest.html) · [Examining the key policy - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/determining-access-key-policy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An airline company uses an ML model to adjust ticket prices according to demand. The model runs on Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints. In prior deployments, the model did not scale quickly enough when website traffic increased, causing delays in ticket-price adjustments.  
  
An ML engineer must configure auto scaling for the SageMaker endpoints so they react rapidly to traffic changes. The solution must use target tracking scaling policies.  
  
Which configuration will be **MOST** responsive to sudden traffic changes?

options.text: Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker AI InvocationsPerInstance standard metric. Configure 10-second interval resolution, and set the default 300-second scale-in cooldown period.
Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker AI InvocationsPerInstance metric. Configure high-resolution 10-second intervals, and set a 600-second scale-in cooldown period.
Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker InvocationsPerInstance standard metric. Configure 10-second intervals resolution, and set a 600-second scale-in cooldown period.
Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker InvocationsPerInstance metric. Configure high-resolution 10-second intervals, and set the default 300-second scale-in cooldown period.

questions.explanation:
`InvocationsPerInstance` is an appropriate utilization metric for target tracking on SageMaker endpoint variants. SageMaker invocation metrics can be published at 10-second intervals when enhanced metrics are enabled, allowing traffic changes to be detected much sooner than the default one-minute frequency. `InvocationsPerInstance` remains a standard metric; AWS documents high-resolution predefined scaling metrics separately for concurrent requests. The default 300-second scale-in cooldown is also less restrictive than a 600-second scale-in cooldown.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatch.html) · [Define a scaling policy for a SageMaker AI endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-add-code-define.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company receives streams of data from devices that monitor patients’ vital signs. The company uses Amazon SageMaker and intends to prepare ML models that predict adverse patient events. The dataset is large and has thousands of features.  
  
An ML engineer must run several hundred training iterations using different feature sets, different algorithms, and numerous possible parameters. The ML engineer must implement a solution that logs the characteristics and results of every training iteration.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to create custom metrics for the characteristics of each iteration.
Write the characteristics of each iteration to logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue and Amazon Athena to search the logs.
Use the SageMaker Model Registry to track the characteristics and results of each iteration.
Use SageMaker Experiments to track the characteristics and results of each iteration.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Experiments is purpose-built to record and organize ML training iterations. It tracks run inputs, configurations, parameters, metrics, artifacts, and results, enabling comparison across experiments without building custom logging and query infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker Experiments - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/experiments-mlops.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is building a fraud-detection model by using the Amazon SageMaker XGBoost algorithm. The model categorizes transactions as fraudulent or legitimate.  
  
During testing, the model performs very well at detecting fraud in the training dataset. However, it performs inefficiently when detecting fraud in new, unseen transactions.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to improve fraud detection for new transactions?

options.text: Increase the learning rate.
Remove some irrelevant features from the training dataset.
Increase the value of the max_depth hyperparameter.
Decrease the value of the max_depth hyperparameter.

questions.explanation:
Strong training performance combined with weak performance on unseen data indicates overfitting. Decreasing `max_depth` reduces the complexity of the XGBoost trees, which helps the model generalize to new transactions. AWS documentation states that increasing `max_depth` makes the model more complex and more likely to overfit.

**Learn more:** [XGBoost hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/xgboost_hyperparameters.html)

questions.question:
An ML engineer must use AWS CloudFormation to create an ML model that an Amazon SageMaker endpoint will host.  
  
Which resource should the ML engineer declare in the CloudFormation template to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: AWS::SageMaker::Model
AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint
AWS::SageMaker::NotebookInstance
AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline

questions.explanation:
`AWS::SageMaker::Model` creates an Amazon SageMaker model resource, including the container and model-artifact configuration that an endpoint can deploy and host.\
\

questions.question:
An ML engineer must use AWS CloudFormation to create an ML model that an Amazon SageMaker endpoint will host.  
  
Which resource should the ML engineer declare in the CloudFormation template to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Use an Amazon Athena CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) statement to create a table based on the transaction date from data in the central S3 bucket. Query the objects from the table.
Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Set up S3 replication from the central S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Object Lambda to query the objects based on transaction date.

Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Use AWS Glue for Apache Spark to create a job to query the CSV objects based on transaction date. Configure the job to store the results in the new S3 bucket. Query the objects from the new S3 bucket.

Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Use Amazon Data Firehose to transfer the data from the central S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket. Configure Firehose to run an AWS Lambda function to query the data based on transaction date.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena provides serverless SQL querying for data in Amazon S3. A `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` (CTAS) operation creates a table from query results and can partition the output by the transaction-date column, allowing date-filtered queries while avoiding infrastructure and custom processing code. AWS Glue Spark jobs, S3 replication and Object Lambda, and Data Firehose with Lambda introduce substantially more operational components; Firehose is designed for real-time streaming delivery rather than processing existing S3 objects.

**Learn more:** [Create a table from query results (CTAS) - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/ctas.html) · [Examples of CTAS queries - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/ctas-examples.html)

An ML engineer uses Amazon SageMaker Canvas to create a custom ML model from an imported dataset. The engineer wants the model to produce continuous numeric predictions using 10 years of data.  
  
Which metric should the ML engineer use to assess the model’s performance?

options.text: Accuracy
InferenceLatency
Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
Root mean square error (RMSE)

questions.explanation:
Root mean square error (RMSE) is a regression metric for numeric prediction. It summarizes the square root of the averaged squared differences between predicted and actual values; lower RMSE indicates better predictive performance. Amazon SageMaker Canvas lists RMSE as a numeric-prediction metric and uses it to evaluate prediction error.

**Learn more:** [Metrics reference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-metrics.html) · [Evaluate your model's performance - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-scoring.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker to fine-tune a large language model (LLM) for text summarization. The ML engineer must use a low-code no-code (LCNC) approach.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Studio to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances.
Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed by a custom API endpoint.
Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances.
Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed by SageMaker JumpStart.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Autopilot supports fine-tuning LLMs powered by SageMaker JumpStart, including models suitable for text summarization. Autopilot-fine-tuned models can be deployed for inference through the SageMaker JumpStart model deployment workflow, preserving a low-code approach without building custom API infrastructure or managing EC2 deployment.

**Learn more:** [Supported large language models for fine-tuning - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-llms-finetuning-models.html) · [Autopilot model deployment and predictions - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-llms-finetuning-deploy-models.html)

A company is developing ML models using PyTorch and TensorFlow estimators with Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer has configured the SageMaker AI estimator and now needs to start a training job using a training dataset.  
  
Which SageMaker AI SDK method can start the training job?

options.text: fit method
create_model method
deploy method
predict method

questions.explanation:
For SageMaker PyTorch and TensorFlow estimators, the `fit` method accepts training-data input and starts a SageMaker training job. `deploy` is used to host a trained model for inference, while prediction methods run inference rather than training.\

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Processing to process and ingest the data. Use SageMaker Feature Store to manage and store the features.
Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to automatically ingest and transform the data. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the features in JSON format.
Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform the data and to ingest the data directly into Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. Use Feature Store to manage and store the features.
Use an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job to analyze, transform, and ingest the data. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the features.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store Feature Processing transforms batch raw data into machine learning features and ingests the resulting values into Feature Store feature groups. SageMaker Feature Store provides the centralized management and storage of those features, with online and offline storage options.

**Learn more:** [Feature Processing - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store-feature-processing.html) · [Create, store, and share features with Feature Store - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must deploy four ML models in an Amazon SageMaker inference pipeline. The models were created with different frameworks. The ML engineer must also enable clients to use the `invoke_endpoint` call to run inference for each model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Create a SageMaker multi-model endpoint.
Create a SageMaker multi-container endpoint.
Create multiple SageMaker single-model endpoints.
Run a SparkML job to generate multiple endpoints.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker multi-container endpoints can host multiple containers that use different models or frameworks on one endpoint. With direct invocation enabled, clients call `InvokeEndpoint` and specify `TargetContainerHostname` to send an inference request to the required model container. Sharing one endpoint improves utilization and reduces cost compared with separate single-model endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI multi-container endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/multi-container-endpoints.html) · [Invoke a multi-container endpoint with direct invocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/multi-container-direct.html)

Which file format meets these requirements?

options.text: CSV files compressed with Snappy
JSON objects in JSONL format
JSON files compressed with gzip
Apache Parquet files

questions.explanation:
Apache Parquet is a columnar file format that supports efficient storage and processing of structured tabular data. Amazon SageMaker Canvas supports importing Parquet datasets from Amazon S3, making it the suitable option for reducing processing overhead compared with text-based CSV or JSON formats.\
\

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure auto scaling on the SageMaker AI endpoint.

Use SageMaker Neo to optimize the model for inference.
Attach an Auto Scaling group to the SageMaker AI endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling dynamically adds instances for a hosted model when workload increases, maintaining capacity for increased inference traffic. It is configured for the endpoint’s production variant through SageMaker AI and Application Auto Scaling.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is fine-tuning an image-classification model that predicts one of two available classes poorly. Analysis shows that the images in the poorly predicted class make up an extremely small portion of the entire training dataset.  
  
The ML engineer must improve the model’s performance.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Optimize for accuracy. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples.
Optimize for F1 score. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples.
Optimize for accuracy. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples.
Optimize for F1 score. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples.

questions.explanation:
For a highly imbalanced binary image-classification dataset, F1 is preferable to accuracy because it reflects both precision and recall rather than allowing the majority class to dominate the metric. Image augmentation can expand the minority class with valid transformed image examples, improving representation during training. SMOTE interpolates feature vectors and is not generally appropriate for generating raw image samples.

**Learn more:** [Metrics reference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-metrics.html) · [Image Classification Hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/IC-Hyperparameter.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer needs to run a training job on Amazon SageMaker AI. The training job will train a neural network using multiple GPUs. The training dataset is in Parquet format.  
  
The ML engineer finds that the Parquet dataset includes files that are too large to fit in the memory of the SageMaker AI training instances.  
  
Which solution will resolve the memory issue?

options.text: Attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS SSD volume to the instance. Store the files in the EBS volume.
Repartition the Parquet files by using Apache Spark on Amazon EMR. Use the repartitioned files for the training job.
Change the instance type to Memory Optimized instances with sufficient memory for the training job.
Use the SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism (SMDDP) library with multiple instances to split the memory usage.

questions.explanation:
Smaller repartitioned Parquet files can be loaded as separate input partitions by training workers, avoiding an attempt to load a single oversized file into an instance's memory. AWS documentation notes that Parquet files are read as partitions and recommends splitting data into smaller files for distributed processing.

**Learn more:** [XGBoost algorithm with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/xgboost.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an ML model that must run once every night to predict stock values. The model receives 3 MB of data collected during the current day and produces predictions for the following day. The prediction process completes in less than 1 minute.  
  
How should the company deploy the model on Amazon SageMaker to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use a multi-model serverless endpoint. Enable caching.
Use an asynchronous inference endpoint. Set the InitialInstanceCount parameter to 0.
Use a real-time endpoint. Configure an auto scaling policy to scale the model to 0 when the model is not in use.
Use a serverless inference endpoint. Set the MaxConcurrency parameter to 1.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference supports request payloads up to 4 MB and invocations up to 60 seconds, so it accommodates a 3 MB input and a prediction that runs for less than one minute. It automatically scales to zero during idle periods, avoiding continuously provisioned capacity for a once-daily workload. Setting maximum concurrency to 1 is sufficient for one prediction invocation at a time.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html) · [ProductionVariantServerlessConfig API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ProductionVariantServerlessConfig.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A government agency is carrying out a national census to evaluate program needs by area and city. The census form gathers approximately 500 responses from every citizen. The agency must analyze the data to derive meaningful insights and wants to reduce the dimensionality of the high-dimensional data to identify hidden patterns.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm in Amazon SageMaker AI.
Use the t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) algorithm in Amazon SageMaker AI.
Use the k-means algorithm in Amazon SageMaker AI.
Use the Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm in Amazon SageMaker AI.

questions.explanation:
Principal component analysis (PCA) reduces a high-dimensional feature set to a smaller number of components that preserve the most important variation in the data, helping reveal underlying patterns and structure.

**Learn more:** [Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pca.html)

A company is collecting audio, video, and text data in multiple languages. The company must use a large language model (LLM) to summarize the collected data that is in Spanish.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Train and deploy a model in Amazon SageMaker to convert the data into English text. Train and deploy an LLM in SageMaker to summarize the text.
Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Jurassic model to summarize the text.
Use Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Anthropic Claude model to summarize the text.
Use Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Stable Diffusion model to summarize the text.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Transcribe converts spoken Spanish in media into text, Amazon Translate translates the Spanish text to English, and Amazon Bedrock supplies a ready-to-use Jurassic text-generation model that can produce summaries without training or deploying a custom model. Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Comprehend do not perform speech-to-text transcription, and Stable Diffusion is intended for image generation rather than text summarization.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Transcribe data input and output](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/how-input.html) · [Amazon Translate supported languages and language codes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/translate/latest/dg/what-is-languages.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer uses Amazon SageMaker to train a deep learning model that needs distributed training. Following several training attempts, the ML engineer notices that the instances are not performing as expected and identifies communication overhead among the training instances.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to **MINIMIZE** the communication overhead between the instances?

options.text: Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in a different AWS Region from where the instances are deployed.
Place the instances in the same VPC subnet but in different Availability Zones. Store the data in a different AWS Region from where the instances are deployed.
Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in the same AWS Region and Availability Zone where the instances are deployed.
Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in the same AWS Region but in a different Availability Zone from where the instances are deployed.

questions.explanation:
For SageMaker distributed training, placing the instances, VPC subnet, and training data storage in the same AWS Region and Availability Zone minimizes network distance and communication overhead between compute nodes and data storage.

**Learn more:** [Get started with distributed training in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/distributed-training-get-started.html)

A company plans to migrate ML models from an on-premises environment to Amazon SageMaker AI. The models use the PyTorch algorithm. The company must reuse its existing custom scripts on AWS as much as possible.  
  
Which SageMaker AI feature should the company use to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: SageMaker AI built-in algorithms
SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker JumpStart
SageMaker AI script mode

questions.explanation:
SageMaker AI script mode runs custom PyTorch training code in SageMaker-managed framework containers, enabling existing scripts to be reused while SageMaker AI manages the training infrastructure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Resources for using PyTorch with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pytorch.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
A company plans to migrate ML models from an on-premises environment to Amazon SageMaker AI. The models use the PyTorch algorithm. The company must reuse its existing custom scripts on AWS as much as possible.  
  
Which SageMaker AI feature should the company use to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Keep all the time-series data without partitioning in the S3 bucket. Manually move data that is older than 30 days to separate S3 buckets.
Create AWS Lambda functions to copy the time-series data into separate S3 buckets. Apply S3 Lifecycle policies to archive data that is older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
Organize the time-series data into partitions by date prefix in the S3 bucket. Apply S3 Lifecycle policies to archive partitions that are older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
Put each day's time-series data into its own S3 bucket. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to archive S3 buckets that hold data that is older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

questions.explanation:
Partitioning the S3 data by date allows Athena queries filtered to the previous three days to prune all other partitions, reducing the data scanned and improving performance. An S3 Lifecycle policy can transition date partitions after the required 30-day retention period to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Separate buckets do not provide Athena partition pruning and add unnecessary data-management complexity.

**Learn more:** [Partition your data - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/partitions.html) · [Optimize data - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/performance-tuning-data-optimization-techniques.html)

A company has created a computer vision model and must deploy it to production on Amazon SageMaker AI. The company has not previously hosted a model on SageMaker AI.  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution to track model versions. The solution must also recommend which Amazon EC2 instance types to use for hosting the model.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Register the model in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use AWS Compute Optimizer for recommendations about instance types.
Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker Autopilot for recommendations about instance types.
Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for recommendations about instance types.
Register the model in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use SageMaker Experiments for recommendations about instance types.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Model Registry registers models as versioned model packages within model groups, providing model-version tracking. SageMaker Inference Recommender runs recommendation jobs and load tests to identify instance types that best fit an inference deployment’s cost, latency, and throughput requirements.

**Learn more:** [Model Registry Models, Model Versions, and Model Groups — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry-models.html) · [Recommendation jobs with Amazon SageMaker Inference Recommender](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/inference-recommender-recommendation-jobs.html)

A company plans to build a real-time analytics application that uses streaming social media data. An ML engineer must implement a solution that ingests and transforms 5 GB of data per minute. The solution must also load the data into a data store that enables fast queries for the real-time analytics.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to ingest the social media data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached).
Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to ingest the social media data. Use AWS Lambda to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the social media data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon RDS.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the social media data. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is designed for scalable real-time data ingestion and can be provisioned or configured with on-demand capacity for the required throughput. Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink processes and transforms streaming data in real time. Amazon DynamoDB provides low-latency access to processed data, supporting fast real-time analytics queries.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage Kinesis data streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/working-with-streams.html) · [Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use Amazon Redshift ML in its primary AWS account. The source data resides in an Amazon S3 bucket in a secondary account.  
  
An ML engineer must configure an ML pipeline in the primary account to access the S3 bucket in the secondary account. The solution must not require public IPv4 addresses.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC with no public access enabled in the primary account. Create a VPC peering connection between the accounts. Update the VPC route tables to remove the route to 0.0.0.0/0.

Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC with no public access enabled in the primary account. Create an AWS Direct Connect connection and a transit gateway. Associate the VPCs from both accounts with the transit gateway. Update the VPC route tables to remove the route to 0.0.0.0/0.

Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC in the primary account. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with two encrypted IPsec tunnels between the accounts. Set up interface VPC endpoints for Amazon S3.

Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC in the primary account. Create an S3 gateway endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow IAM principals from the primary account. Set up interface VPC endpoints for SageMaker and Amazon Redshift.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint lets resources in the primary-account VPC reach Amazon S3 privately without an internet gateway or NAT device. A bucket policy on the secondary-account bucket can grant the necessary permissions to IAM principals in the primary account, enabling cross-account access. Interface VPC endpoints for Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Redshift keep service API connectivity on the AWS network without public IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Bucket policies for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A digital-media entertainment company needs real-time video-content moderation to ensure compliance during live-streaming events.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition and AWS Lambda to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
Use Amazon Rekognition and a large language model (LLM) hosted on Amazon Bedrock to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Comprehend to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Rekognition supplies managed visual content-moderation and image-analysis capabilities, while AWS Lambda provides serverless processing for incoming video frames. This combination supports low-latency frame analysis without operating ML infrastructure. Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Comprehend are intended for speech and text analysis, and building or operating SageMaker AI or an additional Bedrock LLM introduces unnecessary operational complexity for visual-frame moderation. [Amazon Rekognition content moderation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/moderation.html), [AWS serverless video-frame analysis reference](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/create-a-serverless-solution-for-video-frame-analysis-and-alerting/)

**Learn more:** [Amazon Rekognition content moderation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/moderation.html) · [Create a Serverless Solution for Video Frame Analysis and Alerting](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/create-a-serverless-solution-for-video-frame-analysis-and-alerting/)

A company must develop an ML model that identifies an item in an image and provides the item's location.  
  
Which Amazon SageMaker algorithm meets these requirements?

options.text: Image classification
XGBoost
Object detection
K-nearest neighbors (k-NN)

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Object Detection identifies and classifies objects in images and reports each object's location and scale using a rectangular bounding box. This satisfies both item identification and localization requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [How Object Detection Works - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/algo-object-detection-tech-notes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A music-streaming company continuously sends song ratings from an application to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to use the ratings as input for the training and inference of an Amazon SageMaker AI model.  
  
The company has an AWS Glue Data Catalog configured with the S3 bucket as its source. An ML engineer must implement a solution that creates a repository for this data. The solution must ensure the data remains synchronized for batch training and real-time inference.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Ingest data into SageMaker Feature Store from the S3 bucket. Apply tags and indexes.
Use Amazon Athena. Create tables by using CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) queries to group data.
Use AWS Lake Formation. Apply tag-based control on the data.
Use the Generate Data Insights function in SageMaker Data Wrangler.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store provides a feature repository with an offline store for historical data used in model training and batch inference and an online store for low-latency feature retrieval during real-time model serving. When both stores are enabled for a feature group, they synchronize to avoid discrepancies between training and serving data. Feature Store supports batch ingestion from Amazon S3 sources and can use AWS Glue catalog metadata for its offline store.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI Feature Store storage configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store-storage-configurations.html) · [Create, store, and share features with Amazon SageMaker Feature Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to build a classification model that rates the company’s monthly sales performance for each month over the past 20 years on a scale of 1 to 5. The dataset contains fields for month, sales region, regional aggregate sales, and the number of stores in each sales region. The company observes that aggregate sales values are unexpectedly high during two months of every year. The company applies one-hot encoding to every non-numerical feature in the training and validation datasets. The company trains the classification model with the training dataset. When the company evaluates the model using the validation dataset, the results are less accurate than anticipated.  
  
The company must increase the model’s accuracy on the validation dataset.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Remove records that include outliers across all features.
Use a stratified split on the month and sales region features.
Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature.
Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature for each sales region.

questions.explanation:
Aggregate sales should be normalized independently for each sales region because regions can have different baseline sales ranges. Per-region normalization preserves recurring high-sales periods while expressing each value relative to that region’s distribution, preventing larger-volume regions from disproportionately influencing the classifier. AWS documentation describes normalization as feature scaling and notes that it prevents a model from being dominated by the weight of a single feature.

**Learn more:** [How Linear Learner works - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/ll_how-it-works.html)

Which EC2 instance purchasing option will satisfy these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Spot Instances
Reserved Instances
On-Demand Instances
Dedicated Instances

questions.explanation:
Spot Instances provide discounted spare EC2 capacity and are well suited to flexible, fault-tolerant batch workloads that can handle interruptions. The weekend-only job is interruptible, so it can use Spot capacity at a lower cost than On-Demand or Dedicated Instances, without the longer commitment associated with Reserved Instances.

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an ML model on Amazon SageMaker. The company uses an automated process that makes API calls to create training jobs for the model. New compliance rules prohibit the company from collecting aggregated metadata from training jobs.  
  
Which solution will stop SageMaker from collecting metadata from the training jobs?

options.text: Opt out of metadata tracking for any training job that is submitted.
Ensure that training jobs are running in a private subnet in a custom VPC.
Encrypt the training data with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.
Reconfigure the training jobs to use only AWS Nitro instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker supports opting out of aggregate metadata collection for each training job created through the API. Set the `OPT_OUT_TRACKING` environment variable to `1` in the `CreateTrainingJob` request. Network placement, encryption, and instance hardware do not disable metadata tracking.

**Learn more:** [Data Privacy in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-privacy.html)

questions.question:
An ML engineer is developing an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. The engineer must load historical data directly from Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, and Snowflake into SageMaker AI.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to import the data into SageMaker AI.
Build a pipeline in SageMaker Pipelines to process the data. Use AWS DataSync to load the processed data into SageMaker AI.
Create a feature store in SageMaker Feature Store. Use an Apache Spark connector to Feature Store to access the data.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to query and import the data.

A company must deploy a custom-trained classification ML model on AWS. The model needs to produce near-real-time, low-latency predictions and handle changing request volumes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform job to process inference requests in batches.
Use Amazon API Gateway to receive prediction requests. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host and serve the model.
Deploy an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. Configure auto scaling for the endpoint.
Launch AWS Deep Learning AMIs (DLAMI) on two Amazon EC2 instances. Run the instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints are designed for interactive, low-latency inference. Endpoint auto scaling dynamically adds or removes model-serving instances in response to workload changes, allowing the deployment to accommodate variable request volumes. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company trained and deployed an ML model using Amazon SageMaker. It must implement a solution that records and monitors every API call event for the SageMaker endpoint. The solution must also send a notification when the number of API call events exceeds a threshold.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Debugger to track the inferences and to report metrics. Create a custom rule to provide a notification when the threshold is breached.
Use SageMaker Debugger to track the inferences and to report metrics. Use the tensor_variance built-in rule to provide a notification when the threshold is breached.

Log all the endpoint invocation API events by using AWS CloudTrail. Use an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring. Set up a CloudWatch alarm to provide notification when the threshold is breached.
Add the Invocations metric to an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring. Set up a CloudWatch alarm to provide notification when the threshold is breached.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail can log SageMaker endpoint data events, including `InvokeEndpoint` API calls, providing a record of endpoint invocation events. Amazon CloudWatch can monitor endpoint activity through metrics and trigger a CloudWatch alarm when the configured threshold is exceeded.

**Learn more:** [Logging Amazon SageMaker AI API calls using AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/logging-using-cloudtrail.html) · [Amazon SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatch.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company routinely receives new training data from the vendor of an ML model. Every 3–4 days, the vendor places cleaned and prepared data in the company’s Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
The company uses an Amazon SageMaker pipeline to retrain the model. An ML engineer must implement a solution that runs the pipeline whenever new data is uploaded to the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transfer the data to the SageMaker training instance and to initiate training.
Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to initiate the pipeline when new data is uploaded.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has an event pattern that matches the S3 upload. Configure the pipeline as the target of the rule.
Use Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) to orchestrate the pipeline when new data is uploaded.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can send object-created events to Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is a supported EventBridge target. An EventBridge rule can match the S3 upload event and directly start a pipeline execution, eliminating custom polling code and the operational overhead of managing an Airflow environment.

**Learn more:** [Schedule Pipeline Runs - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipeline-eventbridge.html) · [Using EventBridge - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventBridge.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must create a centralized catalog for all of its ML models. The models reside in the AWS accounts in which the company originally developed them. The models are hosted in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure ECR cross-account replication for each existing ECR repository. Ensure that each model is visible in each AWS account.
Create a new AWS account with a new ECR repository as the central catalog. Configure ECR cross-account replication between the initial ECR repositories and the central catalog.

Use the Amazon SageMaker Model Registry to create a model group for models hosted in Amazon ECR. Create a new AWS account. In the new account, use the SageMaker Model Registry as the central catalog. Attach a cross-account resource policy to each model group in the initial AWS accounts.
Use an AWS Glue Data Catalog to store the models. Run an AWS Glue crawler to migrate the models from the ECR repositories to the Data Catalog. Configure cross-account access to the Data Catalog.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Registry catalogs ML models as versioned model packages within model package groups. A model package can include an inference container hosted in Amazon ECR. Resource policies on model package groups enable cross-account sharing and discoverability, allowing a designated account to serve as the centralized catalog while the originating accounts retain their model resources.

**Learn more:** [Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry.html) · [Cross-account discoverability - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry-ram.html)
