questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is preparing data for binary-classification modeling. The ML engineer runs an Amazon SageMaker Clarify processing job, and the bias report shows a difference in proportions of labels (DPL) score of 0.4. The ML engineer wants label occurrences to be equal across classes and decides to use SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the data.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to most of the data to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use random oversampling to increase the DPL score.
Use random undersampling to increase the DPL score
Use random oversampling to reduce the DPL score.
Use random undersampling to reduce the DPL score.

questions.explanation:
A DPL value near zero indicates more equal proportions of positive outcomes between facets. Random undersampling removes samples from the overrepresented category to achieve the desired class proportion, so it balances the data while reducing the DPL score. [AWS: Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-data-bias-metric-true-label-imbalance.html) [AWS: Transform Data—Balance Data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS: Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-data-bias-metric-true-label-imbalance.html) · [AWS: Transform Data—Balance Data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed an XGBoost prediction model to production to predict whether a customer is likely to cancel a subscription. The company uses Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to identify deviations in the F1 score.  
  
During a model-quality baseline analysis, the company recorded an F1-score threshold. After several months without change, the model's F1 score decreases significantly.  
  
What could cause the reduced F1 score?

options.text: Concept drift occurred in the underlying customer data that was used for predictions.
The model was not sufficiently complex to capture all the patterns in the original baseline data.
The original baseline data had a data quality issue of missing values.
Incorrect ground truth labels were provided to Model Monitor during the calculation of the baseline.

questions.explanation:
Concept drift occurs when the relationship between prediction inputs and the real cancellation outcome changes over time. The model’s patterns, learned from the baseline data, then become less predictive for current customers, reducing F1 score. SageMaker Model Monitor evaluates model-quality metrics against ground-truth labels and supports detection of model-quality drift.

**Learn more:** [Model quality — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-model-quality.html) · [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Case Study —  
  
A company is developing a web-based AI application using Amazon SageMaker. The application will deliver the following capabilities and features:  
  
- ML experimentation  
- training  
- a central model registry  
- model deployment  
- model monitoring  
  
The application must provide secure, isolated use of training data throughout the ML lifecycle. The training data is stored in Amazon S3.  
  
The company is experimenting with consecutive training jobs.  
  
How can the company **MINIMIZE** infrastructure startup times for these jobs?

options.text: Use Managed Spot Training.
Use SageMaker managed warm pools.
Use SageMaker Training Compiler.
Use the SageMaker distributed data parallelism (SMDDP) library.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker managed warm pools retain provisioned training infrastructure after a training job finishes and reuse it for subsequent jobs with matching configurations. Reusing the retained infrastructure reduces the time spent provisioning resources, which minimizes startup latency for consecutive training jobs.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker AI Managed Warm Pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-warm-pools.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Which solution would satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use SageMaker Experiments to facilitate the approval process during model registration.
Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking on the central model registry. Create tracking entities for the approval process.
Use SageMaker Model Monitor to evaluate the performance of the model and to manage the approval.
Use SageMaker Pipelines. When a model version is registered, use the AWS SDK to change the approval status to

questions.explanation:
A SageMaker Pipelines workflow can register a model version with `PendingManualApproval`; after review, an authorized user updates its Model Registry approval status to `Approved` through the AWS SDK. Approved model versions can trigger CI/CD deployment, ensuring models are not deployed to production until approval is granted.

**Learn more:** [Update the Approval Status of a Model - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry-approve.html) · [Deploy a Model from the Registry with Python - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry-deploy.html)

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security

options.text: Store the new data in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Create an IAM role for the data science team. Use IAM policies to allow access only by using the new IAM role.
Load the new data into an Amazon RDS database with public access disabled. Share the connection credentials with the data science team in an email message.
Upload the new data into a feature group in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. Enable all Amazon SageMaker AI users.
Store the new data in a local file on each data scientist’s laptop to ensure that only that specific data scientists can access the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can securely store unstructured data, and IAM roles with IAM policies can grant the data science team only the permissions required to access that bucket. IAM policies control which identities are authorized to access AWS resources, supporting least-privilege access control.

**Learn more:** [Identity and Access Management for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-iam.html) · [Access management - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-access-management.html)

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML workloads. The company's ML engineer receives a 50 MB Apache Parquet data file to develop a fraud detection model. The file contains several correlated columns that are unnecessary.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to remove the unneeded columns from the file with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Download the file to a local workstation. Perform one-hot encoding by using a custom Python script.
Create an Apache Spark job that uses a custom processing script on Amazon EMR.
Create a SageMaker processing job by calling the SageMaker Python SDK.
Create a data flow in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Configure a transform step.

questions.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler supports visual data-preparation flows and transformation steps, including removal of unnecessary columns. This avoids writing and operating custom Python, Spark/EMR, or SageMaker Processing code for a small, straightforward data-cleaning task.

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML workloads. The company's ML engineer receives a 50 MB Apache Parquet data file to develop a fraud detection model. The file contains several correlated columns that are unnecessary.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to remove the unneeded columns from the file with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Use zero buffering in the Firehose stream. Tune the batch size that is used in the PutRecordBatch operation.
Replace the Firehose stream with an AWS DataSync task. Configure the task with enhanced fan-out consumers.
Increase the buffer interval of the Firehose stream from 60 seconds to 120 seconds.
Replace the Firehose stream with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

questions.explanation:
For an Amazon OpenSearch Service destination, Amazon Data Firehose can buffer incoming data for an interval from 0 to 900 seconds before delivery. Setting the interval to zero eliminates the 60-second buffering delay; tuning PutRecordBatch batch size also minimizes producer-side batching delay, enabling the lowest-latency option among the choices. [Amazon Data Firehose API Reference: AmazonopensearchserviceBufferingHints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_AmazonopensearchserviceBufferingHints.html)

**Learn more:** [Amazon Data Firehose API Reference: AmazonopensearchserviceBufferingHints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_AmazonopensearchserviceBufferingHints.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must build an AI assistant using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) in Amazon Bedrock. The company keeps a collection of PDF text files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The ML engineer needs to create an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that processes the PDF files and stores the processed files in a vector store.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Use the latest version of Amazon Titan Text Premier to perform document embedding.
Use the latest version of Mistral 7B Instruct to perform instruction tuning.
Use the latest version of Anthropic Claude Sonnet to perform instruction tuning.
Use Cohere Embed Multilingual to perform document embedding.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases require an embedding model to transform ingested document text into vector embeddings for storage and retrieval in a vector store. Cohere Embed Multilingual is a supported Amazon Bedrock embedding model, whereas the listed Titan, Mistral, and Claude alternatives are not the appropriate document-embedding choice.

**Learn more:** [Supported models and Regions for Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-supported.html) · [Embed Multilingual - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-cohere-embed-multilingual.html)

A company uses a compute-optimized instance to run training jobs on Amazon SageMaker. Demand for the training runs will be steady for the next 55 weeks. The instance must run for 35 hours per week, and the company wants to lower its model-training costs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a serverless endpoint with a provisioned concurrency of 35 hours for each week. Run the training on the endpoint.
Use SageMaker Edge Manager for the training. Specify the instance requirement in the edge device configuration. Run the training.
Use the heterogeneous cluster feature of SageMaker Training. Configure the instance_type, instance_count, and instance_groups arguments to run training jobs.
Opt in to a SageMaker Savings Plan with a 1-year term and an All Upfront payment. Run a SageMaker Training job on the instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Savings Plans provide discounted pricing for eligible SageMaker Training instance usage in exchange for a consistent hourly usage commitment over a one- or three-year term. An ML engineer is running a hyperparameter tuning job in Amazon SageMaker AI. The hyperparameter tuning job will train an XGBoost model using a tabular dataset with millions of rows.  
  
Each individual training job is configured to use up to 8 GPU instances, resulting in high costs if too many jobs run concurrently. The ML engineer needs to ensure that no more than five training jobs run in parallel at any time while still exploring all hyperparameter configurations.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set the resource limit for the MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs parameter to 5 in the hyperparameter tuning job.
Set the resource limit for the MaxParallelTrainingJobs parameter to 5 in the hyperparameter tuning job.
Set the stopping condition for the MaxRuntimeInSeconds parameter to 5 in the hyperparameter tuning job.
Set the resource limit for the MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs parameter to 5 inside the script in the hyperparameter training job.

questions.explanation:
In Amazon SageMaker AI hyperparameter tuning, `MaxParallelTrainingJobs` sets the maximum number of concurrent training jobs that the tuning job can launch. Setting it to 5 limits GPU-intensive jobs to five at once without setting a cap on the total number of training jobs or hyperparameter configurations explored.

**Learn more:** [ResourceLimits - Amazon SageMaker AI API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ResourceLimits.html) · [Best Practices for Hyperparameter Tuning - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/automatic-model-tuning-considerations.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is developing an ML pipeline. The pipeline must process a dataset in two ways by using Amazon Athena. It must use batch processing for large-scale data transformations and model training. It must also use near-real-time processing for low-latency inference and analytics queries.  
  
Which file format provides the **LEAST** latency for both processing types?

options.text: CSV
Apache Parquet
Nested JSON
Deserialized JSON

questions.explanation:
Apache Parquet is a columnar format optimized for fast analytical retrieval in Amazon Athena. Its column-level compression, predicate pushdown, metadata-based block skipping, and parallel reads reduce the amount of data scanned and I/O, improving performance for both large batch workloads and low-latency queries.

**Learn more:** [Use columnar storage formats - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/columnar-storage.html) · [Optimize data - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/performance-tuning-data-optimization-techniques.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has created a new ML model. Before fully releasing the model to production, the company requires online model validation on 10% of traffic. The company serves the model through an Amazon SageMaker endpoint behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
Which solution will configure the required online validation with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use production variants to add the new model to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Set the variant weight to 0.1 for the new model. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Use production variants to add the new model to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Set the variant weight to 1 for the new model. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Create a new SageMaker endpoint. Use production variants to add the new model to the new endpoint. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Configure the ALB to route 10% of the traffic to the new model at the existing SageMaker endpoint. Monitor the number of invocations by using AWS CloudTrail.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker production variants provide built-in A/B testing by distributing endpoint invocation traffic among model variants according to their assigned weights. Adding the new model as a variant on the existing endpoint and assigning it a 10% traffic weight avoids a separate endpoint and custom ALB traffic-routing configuration. Amazon CloudWatch provides invocation metrics for monitoring the variants.

**Learn more:** [Testing models with production variants - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-ab-testing.html) · [ProductionVariant - Amazon SageMaker API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ProductionVariant.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company gathers customer data every day and stores it as compressed files in an Amazon S3 bucket partitioned by date. Each month, analysts download and process the data to validate its quality, then upload it to Amazon QuickSight dashboards.  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution that automatically validates data quality before the data is sent to QuickSight.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Run an AWS Glue crawler every month to update the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use AWS Glue Data Quality rules to check the data quality.

Use an AWS Glue trigger to run an AWS Glue crawler every month to update the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Create an AWS Glue job that loads the data into a PySpark DataFrame. Configure the job to apply custom functions and to evaluate the data quality.
Run Python scripts on an AWS Lambda function every month to evaluate data quality. Configure the S3 bucket to invoke the Lambda function when objects are added to the S3 bucket.

Configure the S3 bucket to send event notifications to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when objects are uploaded. Use Amazon CloudWatch insights every month for the SQS queue to evaluate the data quality.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue Data Quality is a serverless managed service that evaluates data-quality rules against AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. An AWS Glue crawler can update the catalog with newly discovered date partitions in the S3 data, allowing Glue Data Quality rules to validate the dataset without maintaining custom PySpark or Lambda code. AWS documents that Glue Data Quality rulesets are associated with Data Catalog tables and that the service supports S3 data sources and scheduled evaluations.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue Data Quality](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/glue-data-quality.html) · [Using crawlers to populate the Data Catalog](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker to develop ML models. The company keeps sensitive training data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Model training must be network-isolated from the internet.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Run the SageMaker training jobs in private subnets. Create a NAT gateway. Route traffic for training through the NAT gateway.
Run the SageMaker training jobs in private subnets. Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint. Route traffic for training through the S3 gateway VPC endpoint.

Run the SageMaker training jobs in public subnets that have an attached security group. In the security group, use inbound rules to limit traffic from the internet. Encrypt SageMaker instance storage by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

Encrypt traffic to Amazon S3 by using a bucket policy that includes a value of True for the aws:SecureTransport condition key. Use default at-rest encryption for Amazon S3. Encrypt SageMaker instance storage by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

questions.explanation:
SageMaker training jobs can run in private subnets without internet access. An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds private routing to S3, allowing the jobs to access training data without using a NAT gateway or traversing the public internet. AWS documents this configuration for training containers that need S3 access while the VPC has no internet access.

**Learn more:** [Give SageMaker AI Training Jobs Access to Resources in Your Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-vpc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must deploy ML models to obtain inferences from large datasets asynchronously. The ML engineer must also implement scheduled monitoring of the models’ data quality and receive alerts when data-quality changes occur.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the models by using scheduled AWS Glue jobs. Use Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
Deploy the models by using scheduled AWS Batch jobs. Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
Deploy the models by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. Use Amazon EventBridge to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
Deploy the models by using Amazon SageMaker batch transform. Use SageMaker Model Monitor to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker batch transform performs asynchronous inference on large datasets without requiring a persistent endpoint. SageMaker Model Monitor can schedule data-quality monitoring for batch transform jobs, detect data drift or constraint violations, and issue alerts when quality issues occur.

**Learn more:** [Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html) · [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html)

A company is developing an ML model using Amazon SageMaker, AWS-owned libraries, and open-source libraries. The company must ensure that SageMaker does not gather metadata about usage and errors while training.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Associate the SageMaker domain with a custom IAM role. Attach the role to a policy that denies Amazon CloudWatch service usage logs.
Add an IAM role to the SageMaker domain to deny Amazon CloudWatch the permission to report metadata.
Turn off the setting in the SageMaker domain to share metadata for console jobs. Opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs.
Set a parameter to opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI, Boto3, or the SageMaker Python SDK.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker can collect aggregate usage and error metadata from AWS-owned and open-source libraries during training. Metadata collection must be disabled for console-created jobs through the console metadata-sharing setting and opted out of individually for every training job submitted through an API, including the AWS CLI or SDKs. IAM policies and Amazon CloudWatch permissions do not control this SageMaker training metadata collection.

**Learn more:** [Data Privacy in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-privacy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must analyze a large dataset stored in Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format. The company wants to apply one-hot encoding to some columns.  
  
The company requires a no-code solution to transform the data. The solution must write the transformed data back to the same S3 bucket for model training.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an AWS Glue DataBrew project that connects to the data. Use the DataBrew interactive interface to create a recipe that performs the one-hot encoding transformation. Create a job to apply the transformation and to write the output back to an S3 bucket.

Configure an AWS Glue Data Catalog table that points to the data. Use Amazon Athena to write SQL commands to perform the one-hot encoding transformation. Configure Athena to write the query results back to an S3 bucket.

Configure an AWS Glue Data Catalog table that points to the data. Create an AWS Glue ETL interactive notebook. Use the notebook to perform the one-hot encoding transformation. Run the configured cells and write the results back to an S3 bucket.

Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster to access the data by using Redshift Spectrum. Use SQL commands to perform the one-hot encoding transformation within Amazon Redshift. Configure Amazon Redshift to write the results back to an S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual, no-code data-preparation service. It supports Parquet data in Amazon S3, includes the `ONE_HOT_ENCODING` recipe action for categorical columns, and can run a recipe job that writes transformed output to an Amazon S3 location, including a location in the original bucket.

**Learn more:** [ONE_HOT_ENCODING - AWS Glue DataBrew Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/recipe-actions.ONE_HOT_ENCODING.html) · [Creating and working with AWS Glue DataBrew recipe jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/jobs.recipe.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to monitor sneaker sale prices over time. The dashboard aggregates sale prices scraped from numerous retail websites. The company needs to identify prices that are unusually high outliers and display those outliers visually.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a vertical bar chart to visualize the outliers. Use a calculated field in QuickSight to take the square roots of the outlier prices to generate the chart. Configure a custom AWS Lambda function to scan the data for anomalies.

Use AWS Glue DataBrew to preprocess the data. Set the REMOVE_OUTLIERS operation to eliminate data rows that include unusually high prices. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to store the removed rows in Amazon DynamoDB.

Use a vertical bar chart to visualize the outliers. Use a calculated field in QuickSight to square the outlier prices to generate the chart. Use QuickSight anomaly detection insights to determine which prices are unusually high.
Use a QuickSight filter to find the lowest 10 values for sneaker price. Assign a specific color to the 10 lowest values.

questions.explanation:
Amazon QuickSight ML-powered anomaly detection identifies outliers in time-series data and surfaces anomaly insights in visuals, eliminating the need for custom anomaly-detection code. A vertical bar chart can display the identified high-price values; squaring the values accentuates their visual separation.

**Learn more:** [Detecting outliers with ML-powered anomaly detection - Amazon Quick](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/anomaly-detection.html) · [BarChartVisual - Amazon QuickSight API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/APIReference/API_BarChartVisual.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon Athena to query a dataset stored in Amazon S3. The dataset contains a target variable that the company wants to predict.  
  
The company needs to use the dataset in a solution to determine whether a model can predict the target variable.  
  
Which solution provides this information with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Create a new model by using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Report the model's achieved performance.
Implement custom scripts to perform data pre-processing, multiple linear regression, and performance evaluation. Run the scripts on Amazon EC2 instances.
Configure Amazon Macie to analyze the dataset and to create a model. Report the model's achieved performance.
Select a model from Amazon Bedrock. Tune the model with the data. Report the model's achieved performance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Autopilot automates the end-to-end AutoML workflow for tabular regression and classification, including data preprocessing, algorithm selection, model training, hyperparameter optimization, validation, and model-performance evaluation. Its reported performance therefore provides the needed assessment with minimal development effort.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker Autopilot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-automate-model-development.html) · [Automated ML, no-code, or low-code](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/use-auto-ml.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a near-real-time data analytics application to identify anomalies and failures in industrial equipment. The company has thousands of IoT sensors that transmit data every 60 seconds. When new application versions are released, the company wants to make sure that application-code bugs do not stop the application from running.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink with the system rollback capability enabled to build the data analytics application.
Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink with manual rollback when an error occurs to build the data analytics application.

Use Amazon Data Firehose to deliver real-time streaming data programmatically for the data analytics application. Pause the stream when a new version of the application is released and resume the stream after the application is deployed.
Use Amazon Data Firehose to deliver data to Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones for the data analytics application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink performs near-real-time stream processing. When system rollback is enabled, it automatically reverts an application update to the prior successfully running version if code or configuration errors prevent the new version from starting, minimizing downtime and preserving continued processing.

**Learn more:** [Enable system rollbacks for your Managed Service for Apache Flink application](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/latest/java/how-system-rollbacks.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to deploy a new recommendation model for its ecommerce website. The model must use data from every client website interaction as input.  
  
Traffic varies during the day. The company must create an inference endpoint for the model.  
  
Which type of inference endpoint will satisfy these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Batch transform inference endpoint
Asynchronous inference endpoint
Real-time inference endpoint
Serverless inference endpoint

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Inference is designed for synchronous workloads with intermittent, spiky, or unpredictable traffic. It automatically scales compute resources in response to request volume and can scale to zero during idle periods, so charges apply only to the compute used for inference rather than to continuously provisioned endpoint instances.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html) · [Inference cost optimization best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/inference-cost-optimization.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores user clickstream data in an Amazon S3 bucket in AWS Account A. The company must use the data to train an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI in AWS Account B. The training job will run for 10 days.  
  
The company must use only private IP addresses for training. It also must ensure that no training metadata is shared with AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set up VPC peering between Account A and Account B. Contact AWS by email to opt out of metadata collection.
Set up a VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket. Set the SageMaker AI OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable to 1 in the training job.
Configure a security group policy that is assigned to the S3 bucket in Account A to allow access from only Account B. Create AI services opt-out policies.

Generate presigned URLs with expiration times for the objects that are stored in the S3 bucket. Access the data by using the presigned URLs. Set the SageMaker AI OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable to 1 in the training job.

questions.explanation:
A SageMaker AI training job in a private VPC uses an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint to reach the S3 bucket without internet access. Setting the training-job environment variable `OPT_OUT_TRACKING` to `1` opts the job out of SageMaker AI training metadata collection.

**Learn more:** [Give SageMaker AI Training Jobs Access to Resources in Your Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-vpc.html) · [Data Privacy in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-privacy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must combine and transform data from two sources to retrain an existing ML model. One source contains `.csv` files stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each `.csv` file contains millions of records. The other source is an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.  
  
The merged output must be written to a second S3 bucket. The ML engineer must run this merge-and-transform task every week.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a transient Amazon EMR cluster every week. Use the cluster to run an Apache Spark job to merge and transform the data.
Create a weekly AWS Glue job that uses the Apache Spark engine. Use DynamicFrame native operations to merge and transform the data.
Create an AWS Lambda function that runs Apache Spark code every week to merge and transform the data. Configure the Lambda function to connect to the initial S3 bucket and the DB cluster.
Create an AWS Batch job that runs Apache Spark code on Amazon EC2 instances every week. Configure the Spark code to save the data from the EC2 instances to the second S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service that runs Apache Spark jobs for large-scale data processing. Glue DynamicFrames support reading from Amazon S3 and JDBC-compatible relational sources, performing joins and transformations, and writing output to an Amazon S3 path. Scheduling a weekly Glue job avoids operating EMR clusters or EC2-based Batch infrastructure, making it the lowest-overhead option.

**Learn more:** [DynamicFrame class - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-api-crawler-pyspark-extensions-dynamic-frame.html) · [GlueContext class - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-api-crawler-pyspark-extensions-glue-context.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's dataset for predictive analytics includes duplicate records, missing data, and unusually extreme high or low values. The company requires a solution that resolves these data-quality issues quickly while maintaining data integrity.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to delete duplicate records, fill missing values with medians, and replace extreme values with values in a normal range.
Configure an AWS Glue job to identify records with missing values, identify records with extreme measurements, and delete the two identified record sets.
Create an Amazon EMR Spark job to replace all missing values with zeros, keep extreme values unchanged, and merge duplicate records.
Use an Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to delete duplicate records, use statistical modeling for missing values, and apply outlier detection algorithms.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew is a serverless data-preparation service that provides built-in, no-code transformations for removing duplicate rows, handling missing values, and treating outliers. It meets the cleansing requirements without operating custom AWS Glue or EMR jobs, while retaining records through appropriate imputation and outlier treatment rather than deleting broad sets of data.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue DataBrew User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/what-is.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineering team works across multiple locations. When the lead ML engineer opens an Amazon SageMaker AI notebook, the engineer cannot see the latest merged notebook that other team members made in a Git repository.  
  
The lead ML engineer must be able to see the most recent SageMaker AI notebook updates.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Run the !git pull origin master command.
Run the !git commit command.
Run the !git push origin master command.
Run the !git branch command.

questions.explanation:
`git pull origin master` downloads the latest commits from the remote `master` branch and incorporates them into the local repository. This updates the local SageMaker AI notebook copy with notebooks that teammates have merged. AWS documentation lists `!git pull origin master` as a Git command that can be run in a notebook cell.

**Learn more:** [Use Git Repositories in a Notebook Instance - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/git-nbi-use.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to offer services that help other businesses label images. It wants its labeling specialists to perform human labeling tasks on AWS.  
  
How should the company register its labeling specialists to receive tasks on AWS?

options.text: Use AWS Data Exchange.
Create and use an internal workforce in Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.
Create and use Amazon Mechanical Turk entities in an Amazon SageMaker human loop.
Use the Amazon Mechanical Turk website.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth supports private (internal) workforces for an organization’s employees or contractors. The company can register its labeling specialists in that workforce, organize them into work teams, and assign Ground Truth labeling jobs to them. [Workforces — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-workforce-management.html)

options.text: Increase the number of training iterations. Retrain the model.
Apply L1 regularization to the training data. Retrain the model.
Decrease the number of training iterations. Retrain the model.
Use SageMaker Debugger to apply L1 regularization to the running model.

questions.explanation:
L1 regularization penalizes feature weights, pushing less useful feature coefficients toward zero. It produces a sparser model that reduces the influence of unnecessary features and helps prevent overfitting; the model must then be retrained with that regularization configured.

**Learn more:** [Analyze and Visualize - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-analyses.html) · [Example: Viewing a Training and Validation Curve - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-valid-curve.html)

A company must use Amazon SageMaker to train a model using more than 300 GB of data. The training dataset consists of 200 MB files. The data is stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage and supplies a dashboard tool.  
  
Which SageMaker training ingestion mechanism is the **MOST cost-effective** solution for this scenario?

options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system
Amazon FSx for Lustre file system
Amazon S3 in fast file mode while using S3 Express One Zone
Amazon S3 in fast file mode without using S3 Express One Zone

questions.explanation:
For a large dataset made up of 200 MB files, SageMaker FastFile is the recommended initial choice: AWS identifies FastFile as ideal for large file containers over 150 MB. It streams objects from the existing Amazon S3 Standard prefix on demand, avoiding the cost and operational overhead of copying or maintaining the data in Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx for Lustre, or an S3 Express One Zone directory bucket. FSx for Lustre is chiefly a consideration for many small files or demanding random-read workloads, while S3 Express One Zone is a higher-performance storage option rather than the cost-minimizing need here.

**Learn more:** [Choosing an input mode and a storage unit - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-access-training-data-best-practices.html) · [Setting up training jobs to access datasets - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-access-training-data.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an Amazon SageMaker AI domain in a public subnet in a newly created VPC. The network is correctly configured, and ML engineers can access the SageMaker AI domain.  
  
Recently, the company identified suspicious traffic to the domain originating from a specific IP address. The company must block traffic from that specific IP address.  
  
Which network-configuration update will meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a security group inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the security group to the domain.
Create a network ACL inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the rule to the default network ACL for the subnet where the domain is located.
Create a shadow variant for the domain. Configure SageMaker Inference Recommender to send traffic from the specific IP address to the shadow endpoint.
Create a VPC route table to deny inbound traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the route table to the domain.

questions.explanation:
Network ACLs control traffic at the subnet level and can contain ordered inbound deny rules for a specific IP address. Security groups provide allow rules only, while route tables route traffic and do not implement inbound deny rules. A deny rule on the network ACL associated with the domain’s subnet blocks the specified source address.

**Learn more:** [Control subnet traffic with network access control lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html) · [Security group rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed an ML model that identifies fraudulent credit card transactions in real time in a banking application. The model uses Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference. Consumers report delays in receiving inference results.  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution that improves inference performance. The solution must also send a notification when model quality deviates.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker real-time inference for inference. Use SageMaker Model Monitor for notifications about model quality.
Use SageMaker batch transform for inference. Use SageMaker Model Monitor for notifications about model quality.
Use SageMaker Serverless Inference for inference. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for notifications about model quality.
Keep using SageMaker Asynchronous Inference for inference. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for notifications about model quality.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker real-time inference endpoints are designed for low-latency, synchronous predictions, making them suitable for immediate fraud-decision workflows. SageMaker Model Monitor monitors production model quality, detects deviations from defined constraints, and supports alerts through Amazon CloudWatch. Asynchronous Inference queues requests for later processing, while SageMaker Inference Recommender recommends deployment configurations rather than monitoring model-quality drift.

**Learn more:** [Asynchronous inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/async-inference.html) · [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html)

A company has trained an ML model in Amazon SageMaker and must host the model to provide inferences in a production environment.  
  
The model must be highly available and respond with minimal latency. Each request will range from 1 KB to 3 MB. The model will experience unpredictable request bursts during the day, and inference capacity must scale proportionally as demand changes.  
  
How should the company deploy the model to production to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a SageMaker real-time inference endpoint. Configure auto scaling. Configure the endpoint to present the existing model.
Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use ECS scheduled scaling that is based on the CPU of the ECS cluster.
Install SageMaker Operator on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Deploy the model in Amazon EKS. Set horizontal pod auto scaling to scale replicas based on the memory metric.
Use Spot Instances with a Spot Fleet behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for inferences. Use the ALBRequestCountPerTarget metric as the metric for auto scaling.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints are intended for low-latency, interactive workloads and support automatic scaling. Their supported request payload size is below 6 MB, so requests up to 3 MB are supported. Endpoint autoscaling adjusts serving capacity as traffic changes, providing managed, elastic capacity appropriate for unpredictable bursts and high availability.

**Learn more:** [Real-time inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/realtime-endpoints.html) · [Supported features - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-deploy-feature-matrix.html)

An ML engineer is training an ML model to identify a person’s health risk using 20 features and 1 target. The target class has two values:  
  
- Likely to have health risk (positive class)  
- Unlikely to have health risk (negative class)  
  
People in the dataset range in age from 30 years old to 60 years old. Age is one of the features.  
  
The ML engineer analyzes the features. For the positive class, the difference in proportions of labels (DPL) value is (+0.9) for the 40 to 45 age range compared with every other age range.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to correct this data imbalance?

options.text: Oversample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
Undersample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
Undersample the positive class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.
Oversample the negative class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.

questions.explanation:
DPL measures the difference in the proportion of observed positive labels between a selected facet and the comparison facet. A strongly positive DPL indicates that ages 40–45 have a higher proportion of positive health-risk labels than the other ages. Undersampling positive-class examples in that age range reduces this overrepresentation and moves the label proportions toward demographic parity.

**Learn more:** [Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-data-bias-metric-true-label-imbalance.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is using a training job to fine-tune a deep learning model in Amazon SageMaker Studio. The engineer has previously used the same pre-trained model with a comparable dataset and expects vanishing-gradient, underutilized-GPU, and overfitting issues.  
  
The ML engineer must implement a solution that detects these issues and reacts in predefined ways when they occur. The solution must also deliver comprehensive real-time metrics throughout training.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use TensorBoard to monitor the training job. Publish the findings to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the findings and to initiate the predefined actions.
Use Amazon CloudWatch default metrics to gain insights about the training job. Use the metrics to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the predefined actions.
Expand the metrics in Amazon CloudWatch to include the gradients in each training step. Use the metrics to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the predefined actions.
Use SageMaker Debugger built-in rules to monitor the training job. Configure the rules to initiate the predefined actions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Debugger built-in rules automatically analyze training tensors and profiler data to identify vanishing gradients, overfitting, and hardware-resource bottlenecks, including GPU utilization issues. Debugger provides detailed real-time training analysis and supports configured actions when a rule detects an issue, minimizing custom monitoring and orchestration components.

**Learn more:** [How to configure Debugger built-in rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/use-debugger-built-in-rules.html) · [Use Debugger built-in actions for rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/debugger-built-in-actions.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer at a credit card company used Amazon SageMaker AI to build and deploy a new ML model. The model was trained using a copy of transactions from the production environment. That transaction copy contained only a small number of fraudulent transactions.  
  
After the model is deployed to production, it is underperforming.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to improve the model's performance?

options.text: Retrain the model with a different built-in algorithm that is available in SageMaker AI.
Use random undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to randomly reduce the majority class samples. Retrain the model.
Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to generate synthetic minority samples. Retrain the model.
Use random oversampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to randomly duplicate minority samples. Retrain the model.

questions.explanation:
A fraud-detection training set with very few fraudulent transactions is class-imbalanced, so the model can become biased toward the much more common non-fraud class. SMOTE balances the data by interpolating new synthetic samples for the underrepresented class while retaining the majority-class data. Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler supports SMOTE specifically for balancing datasets with an underrepresented category, which can improve binary-classification models.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates its ML workflows on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. The ML workflows include ML services that perform training and inference for ML models. Each ML service runs from its own standalone Docker image.  
  
The company must perform a lift-and-shift migration from the on-premises Kubernetes cluster to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Redesign the ML services to be configured in Kubeflow. Deploy the new Kubeflow managed ML services to the EKS cluster.
Upload the Docker images to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Configure a deployment pipeline to deploy the images to the EKS cluster.
Migrate the training data to an Amazon Redshift cluster. Retrain the models from the migrated training data by using Amazon Redshift ML. Deploy the retrained models to the EKS cluster.
Configure an Amazon SageMaker AI notebook. Retrain the models with the same code. Deploy the retrained models to the EKS cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS runs Kubernetes workloads, so existing standalone Docker images and Kubernetes-based services can be migrated without redesigning the ML platform or retraining models. Amazon ECR provides a private registry for the images, and a deployment pipeline can deliver those images to the EKS cluster. This preserves the existing architecture and minimizes operational effort.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon ECR Images with Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/ECR_on_EKS.html) · [Deploy a sample application on Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/sample-deployment.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is gathering data to train a classification ML model using Amazon SageMaker AI. The target column has two possible values: Class A or Class B. The ML engineer wants to make sure the sample counts for Class A and Class B are balanced without losing any existing training data. The ML engineer must test the balance of the training data.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is equal to 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is greater than 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is greater than 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.
Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is equal to 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify can calculate the Class Imbalance (CI) pre-training bias metric. A CI value greater than zero indicates an unequal distribution in which one facet has more samples. SageMaker Data Wrangler's SMOTE operation balances the classes by creating synthetic minority-class samples, retaining the existing training data; random undersampling would instead remove majority-class samples.

**Learn more:** [Class Imbalance (CI) - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-bias-metric-class-imbalance.html) · [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer needs to use, prepare, and load data from Amazon S3 for analytics. The engineer must run an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to discover the data schema and store its metadata.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** manual effort?

options.text: Use AWS Glue to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
Create an Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in an S3 bucket.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that includes the scikit-learn library to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in Amazon Redshift.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue provides a managed ETL service together with crawlers that scan Amazon S3 data, infer its schema, and create or update metadata table definitions in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. This native integration minimizes the operational and custom-development effort required for both ETL processing and metadata cataloging.

**Learn more:** [Using crawlers to populate the Data Catalog - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html) · [Data discovery and cataloging in AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/catalog-and-crawler.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer trained an ML model on Amazon SageMaker to detect automobile accidents from dosed-circuit TV footage. The ML engineer used SageMaker Data Wrangler to create a training dataset containing images of accidents and non-accidents.  
  
The model performed well in training and validation. However, it underperforms in production because image quality varies across cameras.  
  
Which solution will improve the model's accuracy in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Collect more images from all the cameras. Use Data Wrangler to prepare a new training dataset.
Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler corrupt image transform. Specify the impulse noise option.
Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler enhance image contrast transform. Specify the Gamma contrast option.
Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler resize image transform. Crop all images to the same size.

questions.explanation:
Applying the corrupt-image transform with impulse noise augments the existing labeled images with noise-corrupted variants, making the model more robust to camera-dependent image degradation without waiting to collect and label additional footage. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML workflow. A compliance audit finds that an Amazon S3 bucket containing training data uses server-side encryption with S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).  
  
The company mandates customer managed keys. An ML engineer updates the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS), with no other configuration changes.  
  
After this encryption-setting change, SageMaker training jobs begin failing with `AccessDenied` errors.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to resolve the issue?

options.text: Update the IAM policy that is attached to the execution role for the training jobs. Include the s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject permissions.
Update the S3 bucket policy that is attached to the S3 bucket. Set the value of the aws:SecureTransport condition key to True.
Update the IAM policy that is attached to the execution role for the training jobs. Include the kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt permissions.
Update the IAM policy that is attached to the user that created the training jobs. Include the kms:CreateGrant permission.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker uses the training job’s execution role to access Amazon S3 input data. When that data is encrypted with SSE-KMS, the role needs permission to use the KMS key, including `kms:Decrypt` to read the training data. KMS encryption permissions on the execution role also cover encrypted job output where applicable. Therefore, the execution role must be granted the listed KMS permissions for the customer managed key.

**Learn more:** [How to use SageMaker AI execution roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html) · [Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html)

Which solution meets this requirement?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer deployed an Amazon SageMaker model to a production serverless endpoint. The model is invoked through the `InvokeEndpoint` API operation.  
  
The model’s production latency is greater than its baseline latency in the test environment. The ML engineer believes the higher latency results from model startup time.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to confirm or rule out this hypothesis?

options.text: Schedule a SageMaker Model Monitor job. Observe metrics about model quality.
Schedule a SageMaker Model Monitor job with Amazon CloudWatch metrics enabled.

Enable Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Observe the ModelLoadingWaitTime metric in the SageMaker namespace.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a new ML model that uses the XGBoost algorithm. The company will train the model using data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data uses a nested JSON format.

An ML engineer is preparing a medical-record dataset to train an ML model that will predict the likelihood that patients develop a specific disease. The dataset contains numeric and categorical features. The engineer will train the model with a custom container that accesses data stored in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.  
  
How should the ML engineer prepare the dataset for model training?

options.text: Select a random sample of records. Encode the categorical features. Load the pre-processed data into the file system.
Perform data validation to check for missing or invalid values. Encode the categorical features. Scale the numeric features. Select a random sample of records.
Scale the numeric features. Select a random sample of records for the initial model training. Load the pre-processed data into the file system.
Compress the data files. Remove duplicate records. Load the pre-processed data into the file system.

questions.explanation:
ML training data should be checked for missing or invalid values, categorical variables should be encoded into numeric representations, and numeric features should be scaled where appropriate. A random sample can then be selected for training. AWS SageMaker documentation identifies validation, handling missing values, numeric scaling, categorical encoding, and sampling as data-preparation operations.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html) · [Recommendations for choosing the right data preparation tool in SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-prep.html)

A company keeps training data in a `.csv` file within an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to encrypt the data and control which applications can access the encryption key.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new SSH access key. Use the AWS Encryption CLI with a reference to the new access key to encrypt the file.
Create a new API key by using the Amazon API Gateway CreateApiKey API operation. Use the AWS CLI with a reference to the new API key to encrypt the file.
Create a new IAM role. Attach a policy that allows the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) GenerateDataKey action. Use the role to encrypt the file.
Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use the AWS Encryption CLI with a reference to the new KMS key to encrypt the file.

questions.explanation:
A customer-managed AWS KMS key can protect the data-encryption keys used to encrypt a file, and access to that KMS key can be restricted to designated application IAM principals through KMS key policies and IAM policies. The AWS Encryption CLI can use a specified KMS key for file encryption. SSH access keys and API Gateway API keys are not encryption keys, and an IAM role alone does not create or identify the KMS key required for encryption.

**Learn more:** [Examining the key policy - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/determining-access-key-policy.html) · [Using IAM policies with AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/iam-policies.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an ML model using Amazon SageMaker AI. The company must monitor the model for bias and display the results on a dashboard. An ML engineer creates a bias-monitoring job.  
  
How should the ML engineer capture bias metrics for display on the dashboard?

options.text: Capture AWS CloudTrail metrics from SageMaker Clarify.
Capture Amazon CloudWatch metrics from SageMaker Clarify.
Capture SageMaker Model Monitor metrics from Amazon EventBridge.
Capture SageMaker Model Monitor metrics from Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Clarify bias-drift monitoring jobs compute pre-training and post-training bias metrics and publish them as Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Those metrics can be visualized on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer uses Amazon QuickSight anomaly detection to identify machine operating temperatures that are much higher or much lower than normal. The ML engineer sets the Severity parameter to Low and above and the Direction parameter to All.  
  
What effect will the ML engineer see in the anomaly detection results if the Direction parameter is changed to Lower than expected?

options.text: Increased anomaly identification frequency and increased recall
Decreased anomaly identification frequency and decreased recall
Increased anomaly identification frequency and decreased recall
Decreased anomaly identification frequency and increased recall

questions.explanation:
The `Lower than expected` direction identifies only values below the expected baseline, whereas `All` identifies both high and low anomalous values. Excluding higher-than-expected temperature anomalies reduces the number identified and lowers recall for detecting anomalous temperatures across both directions.

**Learn more:** [Setting controls for anomaly detection - Amazon Quick Suite](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksuite/latest/userguide/exploring-anomalies-controls.html) · [Adding an ML insight to detect outliers and key drivers - Amazon Quick](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/anomaly-detection-adding-anomaly-insights.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an ML model that creates text descriptions from images that customers upload to the company’s website. The images can have a total size of up to 50 MB.  
  
An ML engineer chooses to store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. The engineer must implement a processing solution that can scale for changes in demand.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job to process all the images in the S3 bucket.
Create an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint and a scaling policy. Run a script to make an inference request for each image.
Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Karpenter for auto scaling. Host the model on the EKS cluster. Run a script to make an inference request for each image.
Create an AWS Batch job that uses an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Specify a list of images to process for each AWS Batch job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference queues individual requests, supports S3-hosted input payloads up to 1 GB, and can automatically scale endpoint capacity in response to workload demand. This supports 50 MB image inputs and variable upload volume without operating Kubernetes or batch-compute infrastructure. Batch Transform is designed for offline processing of a defined dataset rather than per-image requests as they arrive.

**Learn more:** [Asynchronous inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/async-inference.html) · [Model Hosting FAQs - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/hosting-faqs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer plans to use Amazon SageMaker AI to prepare training data. During exploratory data analysis, the ML engineer finds that several categorical features have missing values.  
  
How can the ML engineer use SageMaker AI to address this issue?

options.text: Use SageMaker Clarify to impute categorical features with the mean value.
Use SageMaker Clarity to impute categorical features with the mode value.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mean value.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mode value.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler includes an **Impute missing** transform for categorical and numerical data. For categorical data, it replaces missing values with the most frequent value in the column—the mode. Mean imputation is for numeric data.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.question:
An ML engineer at an entertainment company is refining an ML model to predict audience preferences. As the model learns from data, the engineer observes that its performance peaks early and then gradually declines. The ML engineer must prevent performance degradation after this initial success.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Increase the number of layers.
Implement early stopping.
Add more neurons to each layer to capture complex patterns.
Examine model bias and variance to understand performance issues.

questions.explanation:
Early stopping ends training when validation performance ceases to improve, preserving the model state from before continued training leads to overfitting and degraded generalization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Stop Training Jobs Early - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/automatic-model-tuning-early-stopping.html)

An ML engineer at an entertainment company is refining an ML model to predict audience preferences. As the model learns from data, the engineer observes that its performance peaks early and then gradually declines. The ML engineer must prevent performance degradation after this initial success.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to deploy the LLM.
Download the LLM as a .zip file. Deploy the LLM on a GPU-based Amazon EC2 instance.
Create a frontend HTML interface that uses an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API with AWS Lambda functions to handle the user interaction.
Use Amazon QuickSight to create a UI to handle the user interaction.
Use Amazon Lex to create a UI to handle the user interaction.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart deploys supported open-source foundation models as SageMaker-hosted inference endpoints, removing the need to operate the model runtime and GPU instance directly. Amazon Lex is a managed service for building, publishing, and automatically scaling conversational text or voice interfaces, so it minimizes custom interaction-layer infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Deploy a Model — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-deploy.html) · [What is Amazon Lex V2?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lexv2/latest/dg/what-is.html)

A company has a data-science team that uses Amazon SageMaker notebook instances to test ML models. Whenever the data scientists require new permissions, the company attaches those permissions to each individual role created when the SageMaker notebook instance was created.  
  
The company needs to centralize management of the team’s permissions.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create a single IAM role that has the necessary permissions. Attach the role to each notebook instance that the team uses.
Create a single IAM group. Add the data scientists to the group. Associate the group with each notebook instance that the team uses.
Create a single IAM user. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed IAM policy to the user. Configure each notebook instance to use the IAM user.

Create a single IAM group. Add the data scientists to the group. Create an IAM role. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed IAM policy to the role. Associate the role with the group. Associate the group with each notebook instance that the team uses.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker notebook instances make AWS requests by assuming their associated IAM execution role. Associating every team notebook instance with one shared role that has the required permissions centralizes permission updates: policies are changed on that one role and apply to all of those instances. IAM groups cannot be attached to notebook instances as their execution identity.

**Learn more:** [How to use SageMaker AI execution roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html) · [CreateNotebookInstance API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateNotebookInstance.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must run intensive model-training jobs every month that may take 48 to 72 hours to complete. The training jobs can be interrupted and resumed without significant issues. The ML engineer has a fixed budget and must optimize compute resources.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Purchase Reserved Instances with a partial upfront payment.
Purchase On-Demand Instances with no commitment.
Purchase Amazon SageMaker AI Savings Plans.
Purchase Spot Instances that use automated checkpoints.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Spot Instances use spare capacity at discounts of up to 90% from On-Demand pricing, but AWS can interrupt them when capacity is needed. Automated checkpoints allow model-training work to resume after an interruption, making Spot Instances well suited to this fault-tolerant, interruption-resilient workload and fixed-budget requirement.

**Learn more:** [Spot Instances - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html) · [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html)

A company plans to use an Amazon SageMaker prebuilt algorithm to build a recommendation model. The algorithm must be capable of generating predictions from high-dimensional sparse data.  
  
Which SageMaker algorithm should the company select for the recommendation model?

options.text: K-nearest neighbors (k-NN)
Factorization Machines
Principal component analysis (PCA)
Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq)

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Factorization Machines efficiently model pairwise feature interactions in high-dimensional sparse datasets and are a suitable choice for item recommendation workloads.\
\
**Learn more:** [Factorization Machines Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/fact-machines.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must encrypt all data in transit while an ML training job is running. The engineer must ensure that encryption in transit applies to the processes Amazon SageMaker uses during the training job.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Encrypt communication between nodes for batch processing.
Encrypt communication between nodes in a training cluster.
Specify an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key during creation of the training job request.
Specify an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key during creation of the SageMaker domain.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker inter-container traffic encryption encrypts communications between ML compute instances in a distributed training cluster. It is enabled for the training job, whereas AWS KMS keys protect data at rest rather than traffic between training nodes.

**Learn more:** [Protect Communications Between ML Compute Instances in a Distributed Training Job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-encrypt.html) · [Protecting Data in Transit with Encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/encryption-in-transit.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must train a supervised deep learning model. The available dataset consists of a large number of unlabeled images that must be accessible only to employees. The ML engineer must implement a solution that labels the dataset with the greatest possible accuracy.  
  
Which combination of steps should the ML engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition to automatically label the dataset.
Train the deep learning model directly on the raw data. Let the model infer the labels by itself.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to create an annotation job that specifies the labeling task and requirements.
Set up workforce teams to access a private workforce to run and review the annotation job created by Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.
Use Amazon Mechanical Turk to complete the annotation job created by Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth labeling jobs define the annotation task, instructions, and label requirements. A Ground Truth private workforce can consist of the organization’s employees and be organized into work teams to complete and review the labeling job, preserving employee-only access while providing human-reviewed labels for supervised training.

**Learn more:** [Create a Labeling Job — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-create-labeling-job.html) · [Private workforce — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-workforce-private.html)
