lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is building an AI-powered traffic-management system that adjusts traffic lights during predicted congestion. The system must use near-real-time inference to produce predictions that help prevent traffic collisions. It must use a batch-processing pipeline for historical analysis of the predictions to continuously refine and improve the model. The historical analysis will require several hours to assess how well the predictions correlate with actual outcomes. The system must also scale inference endpoints appropriately to meet demand.  
  
Which combination of solutions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints. Configure the endpoints to scale automatically based on a target tracking scaling policy that uses the metric ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance.

Configure reserved concurrency for AWS Lambda functions to process streaming data. Use Lambda SnapStart to connect the Lambda functions to Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints to support near real-time traffic predictions.

Configure an Amazon SageMaker Processing job for batch analysis of historical prediction data. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the job to run daily. Allow several hours for in-depth analysis to refine and improve the traffic management model.

Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to host containers to support the batch analysis of historical prediction data. Configure scaling based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze historical traffic patterns and model performance over multiple hours.
Use an AWS Lambda function to perform the historical analysis. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints support online, low-latency predictions and Application Auto Scaling target-tracking policies can adjust endpoint capacity as inference demand changes. Amazon SageMaker Processing runs managed data-processing, analysis, and model-evaluation jobs; these jobs can perform multi-hour historical analysis and can be run on a recurring EventBridge schedule. Together, these services separate scalable real-time prediction from scheduled batch evaluation and model refinement.

**Learn more:** [Auto scaling policy overview — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-policy.html) · [Data transformation workloads with SageMaker Processing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/processing-job.html)

A company is evaluating generative AI and wants to introduce a new product feature. An ML engineer is making API calls from existing Amazon EC2 instances to Amazon Bedrock. The EC2 instances reside in a private subnet and must stay private throughout the implementation. The EC2 instances have an assigned security group that permits access to all IP addresses in the private subnet.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to create a connection between the EC2 instances and Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: Modify the security group to allow inbound and outbound traffic to and from Amazon Bedrock.
Use AWS PrivateLink to access Amazon Bedrock through an interface VPC endpoint.
Configure Amazon Bedrock to use the private subnet where the EC2 instances are deployed.
Link the existing VPC to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Direct Connect connection.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon Bedrock interface VPC endpoint, powered by AWS PrivateLink, provides private connectivity from resources in a VPC to Amazon Bedrock. It creates endpoint network interfaces with private IP addresses in enabled subnets, so the EC2 instances can access Bedrock without public IP addresses, an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or Direct Connect connection.

**Learn more:** [Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is developing a model to predict house and apartment prices. The model uses three features: Square Meters, Price, and Age of Building. The dataset contains 10,000 rows of data, including one large mansion and one extremely small apartment.  
  
The ML engineer must preprocess the dataset so that the model makes accurate predictions for a typical house or apartment.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Remove the outliers and perform a log transformation on the Square Meters variable.
Keep the outliers and perform normalization on the Square Meters variable.
Remove the outliers and perform one-hot encoding on the Square Meters variable.
Keep the outliers and perform one-hot encoding on the Square Meters variable.

questions.explanation:
The unusually large mansion and extremely small apartment are outliers that can distort a model intended to predict prices for typical properties, so they should be removed. Square Meters is a continuous feature that can be highly skewed by large values; applying a logarithmic transformation reduces that skew and makes the feature distribution more suitable for modeling. One-hot encoding is intended for categorical variables, not continuous area measurements.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker Data Wrangler: Transform Data (handle outliers)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has several teams that independently developed separate prediction models on their laptops. The teams created the models by using Python with the scikit-learn and TensorFlow frameworks.  
  
The company needs to rebuild the models and integrate them into an ML infrastructure that it manages by using Amazon SageMaker. The company must also incorporate the models into a model registry.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Export the models from the laptops to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions with SageMaker endpoints to access the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
Import the models into the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker to run the imported models.

Use code from the laptops to create containers for the models. Use the bring your own container (BYOC) functionality of SageMaker to import and use the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
Import the Python-based models into SageMaker. Rebuild the scikit-learn and TensorFlow models in SageMaker. Register all the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker provides managed scikit-learn and TensorFlow framework support, allowing Python model code to be rebuilt and trained without creating and maintaining custom containers. The rebuilt models can be registered as versioned model packages in SageMaker Model Registry. Custom BYOC images and separate API Gateway/Lambda serving components add operational work that is unnecessary for these supported frameworks.

**Learn more:** [Resources for using Scikit-learn with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sklearn.html) · [Resources for using TensorFlow with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/tf.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An IoT company uses Amazon SageMaker to train and test an XGBoost model for object detection. ML engineers must monitor performance metrics while training the model with hyperparameter variants. The ML engineers must also send Short Message Service (SMS) text messages after training completes.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for message delivery.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for message delivery.
Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for message delivery.
Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for message delivery.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker sends training metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, enabling monitoring of performance across training jobs and hyperparameter variants. Amazon SNS supports publishing SMS text messages to phone numbers, making it appropriate for post-training notifications.

**Learn more:** [Amazon CloudWatch Metrics for Monitoring and Analyzing Training Jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/training-metrics.html) · [Sending SMS messages using Amazon SNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sms_sending-overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare analytics company needs to segment patients into groups with similar risk factors to create personalized treatment plans. The company has a dataset containing patient health records, medication history, and lifestyle changes. The company must select an appropriate algorithm that determines the number of groups by using hyperparameters.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set max_depth to control tree complexity for risk groups.
Use the Amazon SageMaker k-means clustering algorithm. Set k to specify the number of clusters.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm. Set epochs to determine the number of training iterations for risk groups.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm. Set a contamination hyperparameter for risk anomaly groups.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI k-means performs unsupervised clustering to group similar records. Its required `k` hyperparameter sets the number of clusters, allowing the company to specify the number of patient risk-factor groups.

**Learn more:** [K-Means Hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/k-means-api-config.html) · [How K-Means Clustering Works - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/algo-kmeans-tech-notes.html)

Allow the bedrock:Get* action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource.
Allow the sqs:ReceiveMessage action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource.
Allow the sqs:GetQueueAttributes action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource.

A company must use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to augment an open-source large language model (LLM) running on Amazon Bedrock. The company's RAG data is a collection of documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. The documents include `.csv` files and `.docx` files.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a pipeline in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to generate a new model. Call the new model from Amazon Bedrock to perform RAG queries.
Convert the data into vectors. Store the data in an Amazon Neptune database. Connect the database to Amazon Bedrock. Call the Amazon Bedrock API to perform RAG queries.

Fine-tune an existing LLM by using an AutoML job in Amazon SageMaker. Configure the S3 bucket as a data source for the AutoML job. Deploy the LLM to a SageMaker endpoint. Use the endpoint to perform RAG queries.
Create a knowledge base for Amazon Bedrock. Configure a data source that references the S3 bucket. Use the Amazon Bedrock API to perform RAG queries.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides a managed RAG workflow that can use Amazon S3 as a data source. It supports both `.csv` and `.docx` documents and manages ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, and retrieval, eliminating the need to operate a custom vector pipeline, database, training job, or SageMaker endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for your Amazon Bedrock knowledge base data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-ds.html) · [Connect to Amazon S3 for your knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/s3-data-source-connector.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must create a processing pipeline that identifies and removes personally identifiable information (PII) from petabytes of unstructured data. The ML engineer will use the processed data to train ML models in Amazon SageMaker AI.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the Apache Spark-based serverless engine from AWS Glue interactive sessions. Use the Detect PII transform feature to identify and remove the PII data.
Use AWS Glue Data Wrangler within Amazon SageMaker Canvas to detect and remove the PII.
Use the Amazon SageMaker Clarify API to detect and mask the PII data.
Use the DetectEntities API action in Amazon Comprehend to identify and remove the PII data.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue interactive sessions provide a serverless Apache Spark environment for data preparation, and the AWS Glue Detect PII transform can identify PII and apply actions such as masking or removal. This supports a scalable preprocessing pipeline whose output can be used to train Amazon SageMaker AI models. [AWS Glue interactive sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/interactive-sessions-chapter.html) and the [Detect PII transform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/detect-PII.html) document these capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Building AWS Glue jobs with interactive sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/interactive-sessions-chapter.html) · [Detect and process sensitive data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/detect-PII.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to build an internal-only chat interface that helps employees respond to customer queries. At present, employees must consult a very large knowledge base of internal documents to resolve customer issues. The new solution must be serverless.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Set up Amazon Bedrock with the Anthropic Claude foundation model.
Set up Amazon SageMaker JumpStart with the Llama foundation model.
Use Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon API Gateway to invoke the model API.
Use AWS Lambda functions with Amazon API Gateway to invoke the model API.
Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store vector database dumps and embeddings.
Use Amazon RDS for MySQL to store vector database dumps and embeddings.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock provides managed access to Anthropic Claude foundation models for the chat capability. AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway supplies a serverless API layer for invoking the model. Amazon S3 provides scalable, serverless storage for vector data and embeddings used to retrieve relevant internal knowledge-base content. Amazon EC2 requires server management, and standard Amazon RDS for MySQL is not a serverless vector-storage choice.

**Learn more:** [Get list of models - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-get-info.html) · [Get started with API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/getting-started.html)

A company is building an ML model for a customer. The company will train the model using data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the customer’s AWS account, called Account A. The company will run Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs in a separate AWS account, called Account B.  
  
The company needs cross-account access to the S3 bucket to train the model. The company has defined an S3 bucket policy and an IAM policy that allow reads from the S3 bucket containing the training data.  
  
Which additional steps will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create the S3 bucket policy in Account Attach the IAM policy to an IAM role that SageMaker AI uses in Account A.
Create the S3 bucket policy in Account A. Attach the IAM policy to an IAM role that SageMaker AI uses in Account B.
Create the S3 bucket policy in Account B. Attach the IAM policy to an IAM role that SageMaker AI uses in Account A.
Create the S3 bucket policy in Account B. Attach the IAM policy to an IAM role that SageMaker AI uses in Account B.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 bucket policy is a resource-based policy and must be attached to the bucket in Account A. A SageMaker AI training job accesses input S3 data by using its execution role, which is the role in Account B where the job runs. Cross-account access therefore requires the Account A bucket policy to grant access to that Account B role and an identity-based policy attached to the Account B role to allow the S3 read actions.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon SageMaker AI works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/security_iam_service-with-iam.html) · [How to use SageMaker AI execution roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)

questions.question:
An ML engineer identifies class imbalance in an image-classification training job.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to address this issue?

options.text: Reduce the size of the dataset.
Transform some of the images in the dataset.
Apply random oversampling on the dataset.
Apply random data splitting on the dataset.

questions.explanation:
Random oversampling replicates examples from underrepresented classes so that training gives those classes comparable representation. Resampling is an established strategy for addressing class imbalance in image datasets.\
\
**Learn more:** [AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate: Data Preparation for ML](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/machine-learning-engineer-associate-01/machine-learning-engineer-associate-01-domain1.html) · [AWS Machine Learning Lens: Address imbalanced datasets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/mlcost03-bp02.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
An ML engineer has trained a neural network using stochastic gradient descent (SGD). The neural network performs poorly on the test set. Training-loss and validation-loss values remain high and exhibit an oscillating pattern. The values decline for a few epochs and then rise for a few epochs before the same cycle repeats.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to improve the training process?

options.text: Introduce early stopping.
Increase the size of the test set.
Increase the learning rate.
Decrease the learning rate.

questions.explanation: A high loss that repeatedly decreases and increases during SGD commonly results from an excessively large learning rate, which causes updates to overshoot a minimum of the loss function. Decreasing the learning rate produces smaller, more stable optimization steps and can allow the model to converge.

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
An ML engineer has trained a neural network using stochastic gradient descent (SGD). The neural network performs poorly on the test set. Training-loss and validation-loss values remain high and exhibit an oscillating pattern. The values decline for a few epochs and then rise for a few epochs before the same cycle repeats.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to improve the training process?

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
Train a Naive Bayes classifier to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
Use random forests to classify sentiments of the chat conversations.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service with built-in sentiment analysis for text documents, returning positive, negative, neutral, or mixed sentiment. It can analyze the chat text directly, eliminating the time needed to build, train, and validate a custom classifier.

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer has created a custom scikit-learn script that transforms tabular data for training a regression model. The ML engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to prepare the data and train and evaluate the model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to run the custom script. Load the processed data into SageMaker AI to train the model.
Use the SKLearnProcessor class within the SageMaker Python SDK to run the custom script.
Apply the HuggingFaceProcessor class within the SageMaker Python SDK to run the custom script.
Use AWS Glue ETL custom recipes to perform data transformations. Load the processed data into SageMaker AI to train the model.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Processing can run scikit-learn scripts to preprocess data and evaluate models on SageMaker AI-managed infrastructure. The SageMaker Python SDK's `SKLearnProcessor` is designed to execute those scikit-learn processing workloads, making it appropriate for the custom transformation script and the associated model workflow.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is assessing ways to deploy an ML model that will be used to generate predictions. The model performs image classification on photos uploaded by customers.  
  
The application using the model requires the model to run with low latency. The company has limited infrastructure-management capacity and must minimize costs.  
  
How should the company deploy the model to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the model on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.
Deploy the model to Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoints.
Deploy the model on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers that run on AWS Fargate.
Deploy the model on Kubernetes nodes on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoints are fully managed endpoints intended for interactive, low-latency inference. They reduce infrastructure-management overhead and support autoscaling, which can help optimize costs as request volume changes.

**Learn more:** [Real-time inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/realtime-endpoints.html) · [Deploy models for inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model.html)

questions.question:
An ML engineer needs to use metrics to evaluate the quality of a time-series forecasting model.  
  
Which metrics are applicable to this model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Recall
LogLoss
Root mean square error (RMSE)
InferenceLatency
Average weighted quantile loss (wQL)

questions.explanation:
Root mean square error (RMSE) measures the discrepancy between forecasted and observed values, with lower values indicating more accurate forecasts. Average weighted quantile loss (Average wQL) evaluates forecast accuracy by averaging weighted quantile losses across the specified quantiles. Amazon Forecast lists both RMSE and Average wQL as predictor-accuracy metrics.\
\
**Learn more:** [Evaluating Predictor Accuracy - Amazon Forecast](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/forecast/latest/dg/metrics.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
An ML engineer needs to use metrics to evaluate the quality of a time-series forecasting model.  
  
Which metrics are applicable to this model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable S3 bucket versioning.
Configure S3 Object Lock settings for each user.
Add cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) policies to the S3 buckets.
Create IAM policies. Attach the policies to IAM users or IAM roles.

questions.explanation:
IAM identity-based policies define which actions a user or role can perform on which Amazon S3 resources. Attaching group-scoped policies to IAM users or SageMaker execution roles can allow access only to the relevant group’s S3 buckets or prefixes while granting no permissions for other groups’ training data. S3 versioning, Object Lock, and CORS do not enforce this identity-based data-access isolation.

**Learn more:** [Identity and Access Management for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-iam.html) · [How Amazon SageMaker AI works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/security_iam_service-with-iam.html)

An ML engineer uses A/B testing to dynamically choose recommendation models. The models are deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints. The ML engineer must monitor system metrics, including latency, call volume, and HTTP status codes, when the endpoints are invoked.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS X-Ray tracing to monitor SageMaker AI endpoints.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch dashboards with AWS Lambda log processors.
Enable AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to track SageMaker AI endpoint metrics.
Deploy AWS Trusted Advisor checks on SageMaker AI endpoint instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI automatically publishes endpoint invocation metrics to Amazon CloudWatch. These include `ModelLatency`, `Invocations`, and `Invocation4XXErrors`/`Invocation5XXErrors`, so a CloudWatch dashboard can present the required latency, request-volume, and HTTP-status monitoring. IAM Access Analyzer and Trusted Advisor do not provide endpoint invocation metrics, while X-Ray is for distributed tracing rather than the native SageMaker endpoint metric set.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatch.html) · [Endpoints monitoring — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/manage-endpoints-console-monitoring.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company maintains an Amazon S3 bucket that contains 1 ТВ of files from different sources. The S3 bucket has the following file types in the same S3 folder: CSV, JSON, XLSX, and Apache Parquet.  
  
An ML engineer needs to implement a solution that uses AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. The ML engineer must also save the final output in Amazon S3 so AWS Glue can consume that output in the future.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use DataBrew to process the existing S3 folder. Store the output in Apache Parquet format.
Use DataBrew to process the existing S3 folder. Store the output in AWS Glue Parquet format.
Separate the data into a different folder for each file type. Use DataBrew to process each folder individually. Store the output in Apache Parquet format.
Separate the data into a different folder for each file type. Use DataBrew to process each folder individually. Store the output in AWS Glue Parquet format.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew can process multiple files in an Amazon S3 folder only when all files have the same format and file extension, so the mixed CSV, JSON, XLSX, and Parquet files must be separated into folders by file type. DataBrew supports writing Apache Parquet output to Amazon S3, and AWS Glue can subsequently consume Parquet data.

**Learn more:** [Connecting data in multiple files in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/datasets.multiple-files.html) · [Product and service integrations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/databrew-integrations.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an Amazon SageMaker domain in a public subnet within a newly created VPC. The network is properly configured, and ML engineers can access the SageMaker domain.  
  
Recently, the company identified suspicious traffic to the domain from a particular IP address. The company must block traffic from that particular IP address.  
  
Which network-configuration update will satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Create a security group inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the security group to the domain.
Create a network ACL inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the rule to the default network Ad for the subnet where the domain is located.
Create a shadow variant for the domain. Configure SageMaker Inference Recommender to send traffic from the specific IP address to the shadow endpoint.
Create a VPC route table to deny inbound traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the route table to the domain.

questions.explanation:
Network ACLs can explicitly allow or deny inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level. An inbound deny rule for the specific source IP address blocks that traffic for the subnet containing the SageMaker domain. Security groups support allow rules only, and route tables do not filter traffic by source IP address.

**Learn more:** [Control subnet traffic with network access control lists - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html) · [Security group rules - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial company receives a large volume of real-time market-data streams from an external provider. The streams contain thousands of JSON records per second.  
  
The company must implement a scalable AWS solution to identify anomalous data points.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Ingest real-time data into Amazon Kinesis data streams. Use the built-in RANDOM_CUT_FOREST function in Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to process the data streams and to detect data anomalies.

Ingest real-time data into Amazon Kinesis data streams. Deploy an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time outlier detection. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect anomalies. Use the data streams to invoke the Lambda function.

Ingest real-time data into Apache Kafka on Amazon EC2 instances. Deploy an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time outlier detection. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect anomalies. Use the data streams to invoke the Lambda function.

Send real-time data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the queue messages. Program the Lambda function to start an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job for batch processing and anomaly detection.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams provides scalable ingestion for high-volume real-time records, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink provides managed continuous stream processing. Random Cut Forest is designed to assign anomaly scores to records in a stream, avoiding the operational burden of self-managed Kafka on EC2 or a separately deployed Lambda and SageMaker endpoint architecture.

**Learn more:** [Migrating Random Cut Forest workloads to Managed Service for Apache Flink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesisanalytics/latest/dev/migrating-to-kda-studio-overview.html) · [RANDOM_CUT_FOREST function reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesisanalytics/latest/sqlref/sqlrf-random-cut-forest.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is deploying a trained model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The engineer needs to get alerts when data-quality issues arise in production.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm and a corresponding action to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification.
Integrate the SageMaker endpoint with a SageMaker Clarify processing job. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to provide alerts.
Configure a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Integrate Model Monitor with Amazon CloudWatch to provide alerts.
Configure a data flow in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Integrate Data Wrangler with Amazon CloudWatch to provide alerts.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor performs production data-quality monitoring for deployed models, detecting data drift and other constraint violations against a baseline. Its monitoring jobs integrate with Amazon CloudWatch metrics, allowing alerts when defined thresholds are breached.

**Learn more:** [Data quality - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html) · [CloudWatch Metrics - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-interpreting-cloudwatch.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company trains a large language model (LLM) using on-premises infrastructure. A live conversational engine uses the LLM to assist customers in finding real-time insights in credit card data.  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution that trains and deploys the LLM on Amazon SageMaker.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Training Compiler to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
Use SageMaker with deep learning containers for large model inference to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
Use SageMaker Notebook Jobs to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker Asynchronous Inference.
Use SageMaker Studio to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker batch transform.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Training Compiler accelerates supported deep-learning training workloads on SageMaker GPU instances, including supported Hugging Face Transformers workloads. SageMaker real-time inference is appropriate for a live conversational application because it serves synchronous, low-latency predictions. Large Model Inference containers are specialized for LLM inference rather than model training, while asynchronous inference and batch transform are not designed for immediate conversational responses.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker Training Compiler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/training-compiler.html) · [Supported Frameworks, AWS Regions, Instance Types, and Tested Models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/training-compiler-support.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to forecast advertising-campaign success while taking each advertisement’s color scheme into account. An ML engineer is preparing data for a neural-network model. The dataset contains color information as categorical data.  
  
Which feature-engineering technique should the ML engineer use for the model?

options.text: Apply label encoding to the color categories. Automatically assign each color a unique integer.
Implement padding to ensure that all color feature vectors have the same length.
Perform dimensionality reduction on the color categories.
One-hot encode the color categories to transform the color scheme feature into a binary matrix.

questions.explanation: One-hot encoding converts each nominal color category into separate binary indicator features, allowing the neural network to use the categorical color-scheme information without implying that one color has a greater or lesser numeric value than another.

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
A company wants to forecast advertising-campaign success while taking each advertisement’s color scheme into account. An ML engineer is preparing data for a neural-network model. The dataset contains color information as categorical data.  
  
Which feature-engineering technique should the ML engineer use for the model?

options.text: Create a multi-container inference endpoint for direct invocation.
Create a multi-model inference endpoint for all the models.
Create a multi-container inference endpoint for sequential invocation.
Create multiple single-model inference endpoint for each model.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints are designed for multiple models that use the same framework and can share a serving container. They share endpoint resources across models, improving endpoint utilization and reducing hosting costs and deployment overhead.

**Learn more:** [Advanced endpoint options for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model-advanced.html) · [Multi-model endpoints - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/multi-model-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company trains an ML model to forecast demand for near-real-time inventory management from historical customer activity. The company successfully deploys the trained model to a production Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. However, it observes that the model’s forecast performance degrades over time. The company needs a long-term, automated solution to mitigate this performance degradation.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to automatically send alerts when model performance anomalies are detected.
Use AWS X-Ray to monitor the performance of the SageMaker AI endpoint and the incoming requests to inform model re-training.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to curate a high-quality dataset. Use the dataset to re-train the model.
Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to monitor model and feature attribution bias to inform model re-training.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify can continuously monitor deployed models for bias drift and feature-attribution drift. These automated drift signals identify changes between training and live behavior and can be used to initiate or inform model retraining, helping maintain forecast quality over time.

**Learn more:** [Bias drift for models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-monitor-bias-drift.html) · [SageMaker Model Monitor - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-mlops.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is building a linear-regression ML model. The model has high accuracy on the training dataset but performs poorly on previously unseen data.  
  
Which action should the ML engineer take to resolve this issue?

options.text: Increase the complexity of the model to capture more patterns in the training data. Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to monitor for convergence issues.
Apply ML techniques such as cross-validation and regularization. Use Amazon SageMaker Experiments to track and compare different model versions and their performance metrics.
Directly deploy the model into production. Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to interpret model outputs on new data. Adjust the model based on these insights.
Increase the size of the training dataset without adjusting the size of the model. Retrain the model on the new data. Generate a confusion matrix to analyze the results.

questions.explanation:
Poor performance on unseen data despite strong training performance is overfitting. Cross-validation evaluates how well the model generalizes across held-out data, while regularization limits overly fitted coefficient values and helps reduce overfitting. Amazon SageMaker Experiments can track training runs and compare their performance metrics.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker Experiments in Studio Classic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/experiments.html) · [Model training - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-model.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An advertising company uses AWS Lake Formation to administer a data lake that contains structured and unstructured data. The company's ML engineers are assigned to particular advertisement campaigns.  
  
The ML engineers must work with the data through Amazon Athena and by directly browsing data in an Amazon S3 bucket. They must be able to access only the resources associated with their assigned advertisement campaigns.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Configure IAM policies on an AWS Glue Data Catalog to restrict access to Athena based on the ML engineers' campaigns.
Store users and campaign information in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update S3 bucket policies.
Use Lake Formation to authorize AWS Glue to access the S3 bucket. Configure Lake Formation tags to map ML engineers to their campaigns.
Configure S3 bucket policies to restrict access to the S3 bucket based on the ML engineers' campaigns.

questions.explanation:
Lake Formation LF-TBAC centrally maps principals and data resources through matching LF-Tags, so campaign-specific permissions can be managed as tags rather than as individual IAM or S3 bucket policies. Lake Formation enforces permissions for Athena and manages authorized access to registered Amazon S3 data locations, which provides a single scalable authorization model for campaign-scoped data.

**Learn more:** [Managing LF-Tags for metadata access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/managing-tags.html) · [Underlying data access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/access-control-underlying-data.html)

A company uses ML models to predict whether transactions are fraudulent. The company needs to detect as many fraudulent transactions as possible.  
  
Which evaluation metric should the company use to assess the models and meet this requirement?

options.text: F1 score
Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
Precision
Recall

Recall measures the proportion of actual fraudulent transactions that are correctly identified. It is the appropriate metric when the priority is finding as many positive cases as possible and minimizing missed fraudulent transactions.\

A company uses ML models to predict whether transactions are fraudulent. The company needs to detect as many fraudulent transactions as possible.  
  
Which evaluation metric should the company use to assess the models and meet this requirement?

options.text: Change to a multi-model endpoint configuration in SageMaker AI.
Integrate Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to manage invocations of the SageMaker AI inference endpoint.
Decrease the cooldown period for scale-in activities. Increase the maximum number of instances.
Increase the cooldown period after scale-out activities.

questions.explanation:
A scale-out cooldown slows subsequent scale-out activities after capacity is added, allowing newly launched SageMaker AI endpoint instances time to become effective before additional instances are launched. Increasing this cooldown prevents rapid, overlapping scale-out actions that cause inefficient provisioning and delays.

**Learn more:** [Auto scaling policy overview - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-policy.html) · [Define a scaling policy - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-add-code-define.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an application that will recommend products for customers to buy. The application will make API calls to Amazon Q Business. The company must ensure that Amazon Q Business responses do not include the name of the company’s main competitor.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Configure the competitor's name as a blocked phrase in Amazon Q Business.
Configure an Amazon Q Business retriever to exclude the competitor’s name.
Configure an Amazon Kendra retriever for Amazon Q Business to build indexes that exclude the competitor's name.
Configure document attribute boosting in Amazon Q Business to deprioritize the competitor's name.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Q Business global controls allow blocked phrases to be defined for an application environment. Amazon Q Business ensures that chat responses do not include configured blocked words, so adding the competitor’s name as a blocked phrase prevents it from appearing in responses.

**Learn more:** [Using global controls in Amazon Q Business](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/guardrails-global-controls.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a real-time data-processing pipeline for an ecommerce application. The application produces a large volume of clickstream data that must be ingested, processed, and visualized in near real time. The company requires a solution that supports SQL for data processing and Jupyter notebooks for interactive analysis.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Data Firehose to ingest the data. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the data. Store the processed data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Use Amazon Data Firehose to transform the data. Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.

Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to ingest the data. Use AWS Glue with PySpark to process the data. Store the processed data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to ingest the data. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to process the data. Use the built-in Flink dashboard to visualize the data.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue Streaming can continuously consume data from Amazon MSK, transform streaming records with Apache Spark, and load the results into Amazon S3 for visualization with Amazon QuickSight. AWS Glue interactive sessions support Jupyter-compatible notebooks, including SQL cells, providing the required interactive SQL analysis capability.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue Streaming ETL jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-job-streaming.html) · [Building AWS Glue jobs with interactive sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/interactive-sessions-chapter.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company shares Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks that can be accessed through a VPN. The company must apply access controls that prevent malicious actors from using presigned URLs to access the notebooks.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Set up Studio client IP validation by using the aws:sourceIp IAM policy condition.
Set up Studio client VPC validation by using the aws:sourceVpc IAM policy condition.
Set up Studio client role endpoint validation by using the aws:PrimaryTag IAM policy condition.
Set up Studio client user endpoint validation by using the aws:PrincipalTag IAM policy condition.

questions.explanation:
Client IP validation restricts SageMaker Studio presigned-URL access to approved source IP ranges by using the IAM `aws:SourceIp` condition key. Limiting access to the VPN’s egress IP range prevents a presigned URL from being used from an unapproved network location.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker Studio Administration Best Practices — Multiple domains and shared spaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/sagemaker-studio-admin-best-practices/multiple-domains-and-shared-spaces.html) · [Connect to Amazon SageMaker Studio and Studio Classic Through an Interface VPC Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/studio-interface-endpoint.html)

An ML engineer must build data-ingestion pipelines and ML model-deployment pipelines on AWS. All raw data is stored in Amazon S3 buckets.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Data Firehose to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
Use AWS Glue to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
Use Amazon Redshift ML to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
Use Amazon Athena to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use an Amazon SageMaker notebook to create the model deployment pipelines.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue creates and orchestrates ETL/data-integration pipelines and can access Amazon S3 data sources and targets. Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic supports SageMaker Pipelines and the ML workflow through model deployment, so this combination addresses both requirements.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/components-key-concepts.html) · [Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/studio.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to introduce a new website feature that predicts home prices from user-provided home attributes. The attributes include location, square footage, and the numbers of bedrooms and bathrooms.  
  
An ML engineer trained a regression model using the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. The model performs well on training data, but it significantly underperforms when validated against real-world data.  
  
Which solution will improve the model’s validation score with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Create a larger training dataset that includes more real-world data. Retrain the model.
Increase the value of the num_round hyperparameter.
Change the eval_metric hyperparameter from Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) to Error.
Increase the value of the lambda hyperparameter.

questions.explanation:
Poor validation performance despite strong training performance is characteristic of overfitting. In SageMaker AI XGBoost, `lambda` is the L2 regularization term on weights; increasing it makes the model more conservative, which can improve generalization to validation data. RMSE is the default evaluation metric for regression, whereas `error` is for classification.

**Learn more:** [XGBoost hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/xgboost_hyperparameters.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy new versions of containers that perform inference to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) compute platform. The ML engineer must define a deployment configuration that shifts traffic to the updated ECS task set. The deployment configuration must shift 10% of traffic to the updated containers in the first increment. The remaining 90% of traffic must shift to the updated containers within 10 to 15 minutes.  
  
Which deployment configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinear10PercentEvery10Minutes
CodeDeployDefault.ECSAllAtOnce
CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes
CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent15Minutes

questions.explanation:
`CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes` is the predefined Amazon ECS canary deployment configuration that shifts 10% of traffic in the first increment and deploys the remaining 90% 15 minutes later. It therefore meets both the ECS compute-platform requirement and the required traffic-shift timing.

**Learn more:** [Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is training a simple neural-network model and monitoring its performance over time on a validation dataset. The model’s performance initially improves substantially, but then degrades after a particular number of epochs.  
  
Which solutions would mitigate this problem? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable early stopping on the model.
Increase dropout in the layers.
Increase the number of layers.
Increase the number of neurons.
Investigate and reduce the sources of model bias.

questions.explanation:
The pattern is overfitting: continued training eventually reduces generalization performance on the validation data. Early stopping stops training when the monitored validation metric no longer improves, and dropout is a regularization method that helps prevent overfitting by randomly setting some units to zero during training. [TensorFlow EarlyStopping](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/callbacks/EarlyStopping), [TensorFlow Dropout](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/layers/Dropout)

**Learn more:** [TensorFlow EarlyStopping](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/callbacks/EarlyStopping) · [TensorFlow Dropout](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/layers/Dropout)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s ML engineer has deployed an ML model for sentiment analysis to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The ML engineer must explain to company stakeholders how the model produces predictions.  
  
Which solution provides an explanation of the model’s predictions?

options.text: Use SageMaker Model Monitor on the deployed model.
Use SageMaker Clarify on the deployed model.
Show the distribution of inferences from A/В testing in Amazon CloudWatch.
Add a shadow endpoint. Analyze prediction differences on samples.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides model explainability through feature attributions, helping stakeholders understand why a model produced a particular prediction. It supports online explainability for SageMaker real-time inference endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html) · [Online explainability with SageMaker Clarify - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-online-explainability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to make its ML operations more sustainable.  
  
Which actions reduce the energy consumption and computational resources associated with the company’s training jobs? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to stop training jobs when non-converging conditions are detected.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth for data labeling.
Deploy models by using AWS Lambda functions.
Use AWS Trainium instances for training.
Use PyTorch or TensorFlow with the distributed training option.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Debugger can detect non-converging training conditions and trigger a training-job stop action, preventing further compute use by an unproductive run. AWS Trainium provides purpose-built training infrastructure with lower energy consumption than traditional EC2 instances, reducing the energy required for model training.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker Debugger](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-debugger.html) · [Guidance for Optimizing MLOps for Sustainability on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/optimizing-mlops-for-sustainability-on-aws/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker and millions of files to train an ML model. Each file is several megabytes in size, and the files reside in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to improve training performance.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Transfer the data to a new S3 bucket that provides S3 Express One Zone storage. Adjust the training job to use the new S3 bucket.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Link the file system to the existing S3 bucket. Adjust the training job to read from the file system.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Transfer the existing data to the file system. Adjust the training job to read from the file system.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) cluster. Link the Redis OSS cluster to the existing S3 bucket. Stream the data from the Redis OSS cluster directly to the training job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre provides high-throughput, low-latency file access suited to ML training datasets containing many files. Linking it to the existing Amazon S3 bucket lets SageMaker use the file system without first transferring the entire dataset to a new storage location, reducing setup and data-loading time.

**Learn more:** [Configure data input channel to use Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-access-training-data-fsx.html) · [Choosing an input mode and a storage unit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-access-training-data-best-practices.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer must implement a monitoring solution that automatically detects changes in the distribution of input data for model features.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor. Establish a data quality baseline. Ensure that the emit_metrics option is enabled in the baseline constraints file. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the company about changes in specific metrics that are related to data quality.

Configure SageMaker Model Monitor. Establish a model quality baseline. Ensure that the comparison_method option is set to Robust in the baseline constraints file. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the company about changes in model quality metrics.
Use SageMaker Debugger with custom rules to track shifts in feature distributions. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify the company when the rules detect significant changes.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to directly observe the SageMaker AI endpoint’s performance metrics. Manually analyze the CloudWatch logs for indicators of data drift or shifts in feature distribution.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Model Monitor data quality monitoring establishes baseline statistics and constraints for each input feature, compares captured inference data with that baseline to detect distribution drift, and can emit Amazon CloudWatch metrics for alarms. This provides managed detection and notification with minimal custom operational work. Model quality monitoring instead evaluates model-performance metrics using predictions and ground-truth labels.

**Learn more:** [Data quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html) · [Constraints schema for Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-byoc-constraints.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker Studio to develop an ML model. The company has one SageMaker Studio domain. An ML engineer must implement a solution that sends an automated alert when SageMaker compute costs reach a specified threshold.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Add resource tagging by editing the SageMaker user profile in the SageMaker domain. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
Add resource tagging by editing the SageMaker user profile in the SageMaker domain. Configure AWS Budgets to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
Add resource tagging by editing each user's IAM profile. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
Add resource tagging by editing each user's IAM profile. Configure AWS Budgets to send an alert when the threshold is reached.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets cost budgets can send notifications when actual or forecasted costs reach or exceed a configured threshold. SageMaker Studio user profiles belong to the SageMaker domain and can be tagged for cost attribution; IAM profiles are not the SageMaker Studio resource used to apply this tagging.

**Learn more:** [Add user profiles - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/domain-user-profile-add.html) · [Managing your costs with AWS Budgets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-managing-costs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a conversational AI assistant on Amazon Bedrock. The company uses Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to refer to its internal knowledge base. The AI assistant uses the Anthropic Claude 4 foundation model (FM). The company requires a solution that uses a vector embedding model, a vector store, and a vector search algorithm.  
  
Which solution will develop the AI assistant with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Use Amazon Kendra Experience Builder.
Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension.
Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension.
Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog metadata repository.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kendra provides managed semantic retrieval for RAG and can integrate with Amazon Bedrock to build RAG chat solutions. Its GenAI Enterprise Edition index uses semantic embeddings and hybrid keyword/vector search. Amazon Kendra Experience Builder can deploy a functional search application without front-end code, avoiding the custom embedding, vector-index, and retrieval implementation required when using PostgreSQL with pgvector.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Kendra works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kendra/latest/dg/how-it-works.html) · [Index types in Amazon Kendra](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kendra/latest/dg/hiw-index-types.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must use an Amazon EMR cluster to batch-process large volumes of data. No data loss is acceptable.  
  
Which instance purchasing option meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Run the primary node, core nodes, and task nodes on On-Demand Instances.
Run the primary node, core nodes, and task nodes on Spot Instances.
Run the primary node on an On-Demand Instance. Run the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
Run the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances. Run the task nodes on Spot Instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EMR core nodes store data in HDFS, and Spot interruption of core nodes can cause data loss. The primary node controls the cluster, so using On-Demand Instances for both primary and core nodes protects the cluster and persisted data. Task nodes do not store persistent HDFS data, making Spot Instances a safe, lower-cost choice for their compute capacity.

**Learn more:** [Configuring Amazon EMR cluster instance types and best practices for Spot instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-instances-guidelines.html) · [Understand node types in Amazon EMR: primary, core, and task nodes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-master-core-task-nodes.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses ML to predict whether a specific weed is present in a farmer's field. The company uses the Amazon SageMaker linear learner built-in algorithm with `multiclass_dassifier` as the value of the `predictorjype` hyperparameter.  
  
What should the company do to **MINIMIZE** false positives?

options.text: Set the value of the weight decay hyperparameter to zero.
Increase the number of training epochs.
Increase the value of the target_precision hyperparameter.
Change the value of the predictorjype hyperparameter to regressor.

questions.explanation:
Precision is the proportion of positive predictions that are true positives. Raising `target_precision` requires a higher precision level when selecting the classifier, reducing positive predictions that are false positives. Amazon SageMaker documents `target_precision` for `recall_at_target_precision`, where precision is held at the specified value while recall is maximized.

**Learn more:** [Linear learner hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/ll_hyperparameters.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built, trained, and tuned two new ML models:  
  
- Model A determines whether a transaction is fraudulent using the IP address, location, and user credentials. This model will be accessed every time a transaction takes place.  
- Model B predicts sales totals for the following month using historical sales data. This model will be accessed once each month.  
  
The company must deploy both models to production by using Amazon SageMaker AI.  
  
Which model-hosting solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Host both models in one container behind one real-time endpoint.
Host Model A with an asynchronous endpoint. Host Model B with a real-time endpoint.
Host Model A with a real-time endpoint. Use batch transform for Model B.
Use batch transform for Model A. Host Model B with an asynchronous endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoints are intended for persistent, per-request predictions with low-latency requirements, which suits transaction fraud detection. Batch Transform is intended for offline predictions over a dataset when a persistent endpoint is unnecessary, which suits a monthly sales forecast generated from historical data. [Model deployment options in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/how-it-works-deployment.html)

**Learn more:** [Model deployment options in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/how-it-works-deployment.html) · [Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker to build ML models. The company’s data scientists require fine-grained control over the ML workflows they orchestrate. They also need to visualize SageMaker jobs and workflows as a directed acyclic graph (DAG). The data scientists must retain a running history of model discovery experiments and establish model governance for audit and compliance verification.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CodePipeline and its integration with SageMaker Studio to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.

Use AWS CodePipeline and its integration with SageMaker Experiments to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker Experiments for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.

Use SageMaker Pipelines and its integration with SageMaker Studio to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.

Use SageMaker Pipelines and its integration with SageMaker Experiments to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker Experiments for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is purpose-built to orchestrate ML workflows as interconnected DAG steps and integrates with SageMaker Studio for graph visualization. SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking records ML workflow metadata, including experiment history, and supports model governance by tracking lineage artifacts for auditing and compliance verification.

**Learn more:** [Pipelines overview - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines-overview.html) · [Amazon SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/lineage-tracking.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an ML model to detect defects in a product. The company has collected a dataset and stored it in TIFF format in Amazon S3. The dataset includes 200 images where the most common defects are visible. It also includes 1,800 images where no defect is visible.  
  
An ML engineer trains the model and observes poor performance for some classes. The ML engineer determines that the dataset has a class-imbalance problem.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to resolve this problem?

options.text: Use a few hundred images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model.
Undersample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible.
Oversample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible.
Use all 2,000 images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model.

questions.explanation:
The defect-visible images are the underrepresented class. Oversampling this minority class increases its influence during training, helping the model learn to recognize defects instead of favoring the much more frequent no-defect class. AWS documentation describes random oversampling as duplicating samples from the minority category to balance a dataset.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows

options.text: Manually install the libraries in the SageMaker containers.
Build a custom Docker container that includes the required libraries. Host the container in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use the ECR image in the SageMaker jobs and pipelines.

Create a SageMaker notebook instance to host the jobs. Create an AWS Lambda function to install the libraries on the notebook instance when the notebook instance starts. Configure the SageMaker jobs and pipelines to run on the notebook instance.
Run code for the libraries externally on Amazon EC2 instances. Store the results in Amazon S3. Import the results into the SageMaker jobs and pipelines.

questions.explanation:
A custom Docker image packages the required libraries once and can be reused as the execution image for SageMaker processing jobs, training jobs, and the corresponding pipeline steps. SageMaker supports bringing custom containers for processing and training, with images stored in Amazon ECR, which provides a consistent dependency environment without separate external compute or per-job manual installation.

**Learn more:** [How to Build Your Own Processing Container (Advanced Scenario)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/build-your-own-processing-container.html) · [Adapting your own training container](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/adapt-training-container.html)

A company has an application that uses various APIs to create embeddings from input text. The company must implement a solution that automatically rotates the API tokens every 3 months.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Store the tokens in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the rotation.
Store the tokens in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the rotation.
Store the tokens in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use an AWS managed key to perform the rotation.
Store the tokens in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use an AWS owned key to perform the rotation.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is designed to store application secrets such as API tokens and supports scheduled automatic rotation through an AWS Lambda rotation function. The rotation function can obtain a new token from the API provider and update the secret on the configured three-month schedule.

**Learn more:** [Rotation by Lambda function - AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_lambda.html) · [Set up automatic rotation for non-database AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-other.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to lower the cost of its containerized ML applications. The applications use ML models that run on Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The EC2 and ECS workloads use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to store predictions and artifacts.  
  
An ML engineer must identify resources that are being used inefficiently and generate recommendations to reduce their cost.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Create code to evaluate each instance's memory and compute usage.
Add cost allocation tags to the resources. Activate the tags in AWS Billing and Cost Management.
Check AWS CloudTrail event history for the creation of the resources.
Run AWS Compute Optimizer.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer evaluates resource configuration and utilization to identify inefficient resources and generate cost and performance optimization recommendations. It supports Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon EBS volumes, eliminating the need to build custom utilization-analysis code.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Compute Optimizer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html) · [Viewing Amazon EBS volume recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/view-ebs-recommendations.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is configuring a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline for an ML workflow in Amazon SageMaker AI. The pipeline must automatically retrain, test, and deploy a model whenever new data is uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The new data files are approximately 10 GB in size. The ML engineer needs to track model versions for auditing.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CodePipeline. Amazon S3, and AWS CodeBuild to retrain and deploy the model automatically and to track model versions.
Use SageMaker Pipelines with the SageMaker Model Registry to orchestrate model training and version tracking.
Create an AWS Lambda function to re-train and deploy the model. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function. Reference the Lambda logs to track model versions.
Use SageMaker AI notebook instances to manually re-train and deploy the model when needed. Reference AWS CloudTrail logs to track model versions.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Pipelines orchestrates end-to-end ML workflows, including data processing, training, evaluation, model registration, and deployment. The SageMaker Model Registry registers each retrained model as a versioned model package in a model group, preserving metadata and lineage for auditing. S3 event-driven initiation can start the pipeline while the approximately 10 GB training data remains in S3 for SageMaker processing and training jobs.

**Learn more:** [Pipelines - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines.html) · [Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A credit card company runs a fraud-detection model in production on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The company has developed a new version of that model and must evaluate its performance using live data without affecting production end users.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set up SageMaker Debugger and create a custom rule.
Set up blue/green deployments with all-at-once traffic shifting.
Set up blue/green deployments with canary traffic shifting.
Set up shadow testing with a shadow variant of the new model.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker shadow testing deploys the candidate model as a shadow variant and sends it replicated live inference requests while only the production variant’s responses are returned to callers. This permits performance evaluation with production data without affecting end users.

**Learn more:** [Shadow tests - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests.html) · [Validation of models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-validation.html)

An ML engineer is working on a project to predict customer churn. The dataset contains customer information and is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A small number of rows have blank values in the monthly spend column.  
  
The ML engineer must replace the blank values with the column’s mean value. The replacement must occur as part of an automated data-preparation pipeline.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to prepare the data?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena with a SQL query that uses the AVG function and an UPDATE operation to replace the missing values.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew with the impute missing values transformation to replace the missing values.
Use Amazon Quick Suite (previously known as Amazon QuickSight) with the Calculated Field feature to replace the missing values.
Use AWS Glue with the DropColumns transformation to replace the missing values.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew supports data-quality recipe steps that populate missing values, including filling missing numeric values with the column average. A DataBrew recipe can be run as a job, making mean imputation part of an automated data-preparation pipeline.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue DataBrew data quality recipe steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/recipe-actions.data-quality.html)
