A company is training a new ML model to replace a model deployed on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. An ML engineer must determine the new model’s latency and accuracy. The ML engineer must assess the new model in a production scenario without impacting users of the existing model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Perform a blue/green deployment with linear traffic shifting.
Perform a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting.
Perform a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size of 50% of the current fleet.
Perform shadow testing with a traffic sampling percentage of 100%.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker AI shadow testing replicates production inference requests to a shadow variant while the production variant continues to return the only responses seen by users. Setting traffic sampling to 100% sends every production request to the new model, enabling production-scale latency measurement and offline comparison of its outputs for accuracy without user impact.

**Learn more:** [Create a shadow test - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests-create.html) · [Best practices - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests-best-practices.html)

An ML engineer must encrypt network communications between the instances that run distributed jobs. The ML engineer configures the distributed jobs to run in a private VPC.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to satisfy the encryption requirement?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company is building an AI-powered assistant for its customers. The company has a large collection of documentation that the assistant must use for general inquiries. The company requires that any responses about prices use only documentation less than 1 month old.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Q Business to develop the responses. Configure a document attribute filter so that responses about prices use only the documents from the past month.
Use Amazon Q Business to develop the responses. Configure the source attribution citation so that responses about prices use only the documents from the past month.
Segment the documents into folders based on the month of document creation. Configure Amazon Q Developer to use only the documents from the past month to develop responses about prices.

Segment the documents into folders based on the month of document creation. Grant the assistant access to only the documents from the past month for responses about prices. Use Amazon Q Developer to develop the responses.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Q Business can generate responses from indexed organizational documentation and filter chat responses using mapped document attributes or metadata. A date-based document attribute filter can limit the retrieval context for price-related responses to documents from the previous month, preserving freshness while allowing the full document collection for general inquiries.

**Learn more:** [Filtering chat responses using document attributes and metadata - Amazon Q Business](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/metadata-filtering.html) · [Document attributes in Amazon Q Business](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/doc-attributes.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a data-ingestion process for an ML model on an Amazon EMR cluster. An ML engineer observes that processing time is increasing.  
  
Which solution will reduce the processing time in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Use Spot Instances to increase the number of primary nodes.
Use Spot Instances to increase the number of core nodes.
Use Spot Instances to increase the number of task nodes.
Use On-Demand Instances to increase the number of core nodes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EMR task nodes add compute capacity for parallel workloads without storing data in HDFS. Spot Instances are commonly used for task nodes because their interruption does not cause persistent HDFS data loss, making additional Spot task nodes a cost-effective way to increase processing capacity. Core nodes also store HDFS data, so using Spot Instances for them carries a data-loss risk; primary nodes coordinate the cluster rather than providing scalable task-processing capacity.

**Learn more:** [Configuring Amazon EMR cluster instance types and best practices for Spot instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-instances-guidelines.html) · [Understand node types in Amazon EMR: primary, core, and task nodes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-master-core-task-nodes.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to train an artificial neural network. The neural network converges more quickly than expected during training, and the model is underfitting. Memory utilization on the underlying training instance is already at its maximum level.  
  
Which modification will improve the model's training results?

options.text: Increase the batch size.
Reduce the number of training epochs.
Reduce the number of images in the training dataset.
Reduce the batch size.

questions.explanation:
Reducing the batch size decreases the memory required for each training step and increases the number of gradient updates per epoch. This can help an underfitting neural network learn more effectively while respecting an instance whose available memory is already fully utilized. Larger batch sizes consume more memory, whereas fewer epochs or fewer training images further reduce the opportunity to learn.

**Learn more:** [Object Detection Hyperparameters - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/object-detection-api-config.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer developed a binary-classification model outside Amazon SageMaker. The ML engineer needs to make the model available to a SageMaker Canvas user for further tuning.  
  
The model artifacts are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The ML engineer and the Canvas user belong to the same SageMaker domain.  
  
Which combination of requirements must be satisfied for the ML engineer to share the model with the Canvas user? (Choose two.)

options.text: The ML engineer and the Canvas user must be in separate SageMaker domains.
The Canvas user must have permissions to access the S3 bucket where the model artifacts are stored.
The model must be registered in the SageMaker Model Registry.
The ML engineer must host the model on AWS Marketplace.
The ML engineer must deploy the model to a SageMaker endpoint.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Model Registry provides the mechanism for cataloging and sharing a model trained outside Canvas so that Canvas can access it. The Canvas user also requires permission to retrieve the model artifacts from their Amazon S3 bucket. An endpoint is for serving inference, not for importing or tuning the model in Canvas.

**Learn more:** [Guidance for Bringing Your Own Machine Learning Models into Amazon SageMaker Canvas](https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/guidance/bringing-your-own-machine-learning-models-into-amazon-sagemaker-canvas/) · [Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A logistics company has deployed in-vehicle cameras for basic monitoring of its drivers. The company wants to enhance driver safety by detecting distractions that could cause accidents.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition eye gaze direction detection to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI to customize an AI model to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
Integrate a third-party driver monitoring system with Amazon Rekognition to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions
Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze text-based driver feedback and identify distractions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Rekognition includes prebuilt facial analysis that returns a person’s eye-gaze direction from images, enabling camera-based detection of driver inattention without building or operating a custom model. Amazon SageMaker AI would require model development and lifecycle management, while a third-party integration adds operational complexity. [AWS: Understanding Rekognition's types of analysis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/how-it-works-types.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS: Understanding Rekognition's types of analysis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/how-it-works-types.html)

An ML engineer receives datasets containing missing values, duplicates, and extreme outliers. The ML engineer needs to consolidate these datasets into one data frame and prepare the data for ML.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to import the datasets and to consolidate them into a single data frame. Use the cleansing and enrichment functionalities to prepare the data.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to import the datasets and to consolidate them into a single data frame. Use the human-in-the-loop capability to prepare the data.
Manually import and merge the datasets. Consolidate the datasets into a single data frame. Use Amazon Q Developer to generate code snippets that will prepare the data.
Manually import and merge the datasets. Consolidate the datasets into a single data frame. Use Amazon SageMaker data labeling to prepare the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler provides an end-to-end workflow to import and combine datasets into a joined or concatenated data frame, then clean and transform the data for machine learning. Its built-in transformations support handling missing values and outliers, and its row-management transformations can remove duplicate rows. [Prepare ML Data with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html) [Transform Data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

**Learn more:** [Prepare ML Data with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html) · [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an ML model to forecast future values from time series data. The dataset contains historical measurements gathered at regular intervals and categorical features. The model must predict future values using past patterns and trends.  
  
Which algorithm and hyperparameters should the company use to build the model?

options.text: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set the scale_pos_weight hyperparameter to adjust for class imbalance.
Use k-means clustering with k to specify the number of clusters.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm with matching context_length and prediction_length hyperparameters.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm with contamination to set the expected proportion of anomalies.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR is a time-series forecasting algorithm that learns from prior observations and supports categorical features. Its `context_length` controls the historical window available to the model, while `prediction_length` sets the number of future time steps to forecast; the context length should be approximately the prediction length. [Use the SageMaker AI DeepAR forecasting algorithm](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deepar.html)

**Learn more:** [Use the SageMaker AI DeepAR forecasting algorithm](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deepar.html) · [DeepAR Hyperparameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deepar_hyperparameters.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must extract entities from a PDF document in order to build a classifier model.  
  
Which solution extracts and stores the entities in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.
Use an open source AI optical character recognition (OCR) tool on Amazon SageMaker to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon Textract to extract the entities. Use Amazon Comprehend to convert the entities to text. Store the output in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon Textract integrated with Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend provides managed named-entity recognition and supports PDF input for custom entity recognition, including document text extraction when needed. Sending its entity-detection output directly to Amazon S3 avoids operating an OCR model, an extra Textract-processing stage, and human review, minimizing implementation and processing time.

**Learn more:** [Document processing - Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/idp.html) · [Entities - Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/how-entities.html)

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed an ML model that uses the XGBoost algorithm to predict product failures. The model is hosted on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint and trained on normal operating data. An AWS Lambda function supplies predictions to the company’s application.  
  
An ML engineer needs to implement a solution that uses incoming live data to identify declining model accuracy over time.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to create a dashboard that monitors real-time inference data and model predictions. Use the dashboard to detect drift.
Modify the Lambda function to calculate model drift by using real-time inference data and model predictions. Program the Lambda function to send alerts.
Schedule a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Use the job to detect drift by analyzing the live data against a baseline of the training data statistics and constraints.
Schedule a monitoring job in SageMaker Debugger. Use the job to detect drift by analyzing the live data against a baseline of the training data statistics and constraints.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor can run on a schedule against captured real-time endpoint data and compare it with baseline statistics and constraints generated from the training data. It is designed to detect data and model-quality drift and report violations, enabling detection of production behavior that has diverged from the trained baseline.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Model Monitor FAQs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-faqs.html)

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a predictive ML model to production using Amazon SageMaker. The company uses SageMaker Model Monitor for the model. After updating the model, an ML engineer observes data-quality issues in the Model Monitor checks.  
  
What should the ML engineer do to mitigate the data-quality issues that Model Monitor identified?

options.text: Adjust the model's parameters and hyperparameters.
Initiate a manual Model Monitor job that uses the most recent production data.
Create a new baseline from the latest dataset. Update Model Monitor to use the new baseline for evaluations.
Include additional data in the existing training set for the model. Retrain and redeploy the model.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Model Monitor compares production data with the statistics and constraints in its baseline. A model update can require a baseline derived from the latest dataset, so creating a new baseline and configuring Model Monitor to evaluate against it establishes appropriate data-quality thresholds.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Create a Baseline - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-create-baseline.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates Amazon SageMaker ML models on accelerated instances. The models need real-time responses, and every model has distinct scaling requirements. The company must prevent cold starts for the models.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint for each model. Use provisioned concurrency for the endpoints.
Create a SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint for each model. Create an auto scaling policy for each endpoint.

Create a SageMaker endpoint. Create an inference component for each model. In the inference component settings, specify the newly created endpoint. Create an auto scaling policy for each inference component. Set the parameter for the minimum number of copies to at least 1.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Store all the model artifacts in the S3 bucket. Create a SageMaker multi-model endpoint. Point the endpoint to the S3 bucket. Create an auto scaling policy for the endpoint. Set the parameter for the minimum number of copies to at least 1.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker real-time inference components let multiple models share an endpoint while independently defining each model’s CPU, memory, and accelerator requirements and scaling each model’s copies separately. A minimum copy count of at least 1 keeps a model copy loaded, preventing a cold start while retaining independent per-model scaling.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models for real-time inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/realtime-endpoints-deploy-models.html) · [CreateInferenceComponent - Amazon SageMaker API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateInferenceComponent.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer chooses Amazon SageMaker AI automated model tuning (AMT) for hyperparameter optimization (HPO). The engineer needs a tuning strategy that uses regression to gradually and sequentially choose the next set of hyperparameters using results from prior runs. The strategy must support small hyperparameter ranges.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Grid search
Random search
Bayesian optimization
Hyperband

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI Bayesian optimization treats hyperparameter tuning as a regression problem. It uses the outcomes of prior training jobs to select the next hyperparameter configurations, making progressively informed sequential choices; AWS recommends it as an option for smaller training jobs.

**Learn more:** [Understand the hyperparameter tuning strategies available in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/automatic-model-tuning-how-it-works.html) · [Best Practices for Hyperparameter Tuning - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/automatic-model-tuning-considerations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an AWS Lambda function to monitor metrics from an ML model. An ML engineer must implement a solution that sends an email message when the metrics exceed a threshold.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Log the metrics from the Lambda function to AWS CloudTrail. Configure a CloudTrail trail to send the email message.
Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudFront. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send the email message.
Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudWatch. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to send the email message.
Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudWatch. Configure an Amazon CloudFront rule to send the email message.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch can receive metrics emitted by a Lambda function and evaluate them with a CloudWatch alarm against a defined threshold. When the alarm enters the ALARM state, it can notify an Amazon SNS topic with an email subscription. AWS CloudTrail records API activity, and Amazon CloudFront is not a metric-alarming service. [Using CloudWatch metrics with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-metrics.html) and [Metrics concepts — Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts.html) describe Lambda metric monitoring and alarm notifications.

**Learn more:** [Using CloudWatch metrics with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-metrics.html) · [Metrics concepts — Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company is using AWS to develop a tool that recommends treatments for patients. The company has acquired health records and self-reported textual information in English from patients. The company needs to use this information to obtain insight into the patients.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker to build a recurrent neural network (RNN) to summarize the data.
Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to summarize the data.
Use Amazon Kendra to create a quick-search tool to query the data.
Use the Amazon SageMaker Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq) algorithm to create a text summary from the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend Medical uses pre-trained NLP models to analyze English unstructured clinical text and return useful medical information, including conditions, medications, treatments, tests, and protected health information. It therefore provides clinical insight without the training data, model design, and training effort required for custom SageMaker RNN or sequence-to-sequence models; Amazon Kendra primarily provides search capabilities.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Comprehend Medical works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend-medical/latest/dev/comprehendmedical-howitworks.html) · [Text analysis API operations - Amazon Comprehend Medical](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend-medical/latest/dev/comprehendmedical-textanalysis.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer used Amazon SageMaker Studio to train a neural network. The network records its information in TensorBoard and uses stochastic gradient descent (SGD) as its optimizer.  
  
The ML engineer reviewed the training graphs and found that accuracy was not increasing and loss was declining very slowly. The ML engineer must improve the model’s performance without increasing the overall training time.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Increase the initial learning rate.
Decrease the initial learning rate.
Increase the total number of epochs.
Decrease the total number of epochs.

questions.explanation:
The learning rate sets the size of each SGD parameter update. When loss decreases very slowly, increasing an insufficient initial learning rate can make training converge faster during the same number of epochs, without extending total training time. Increasing the number of epochs would increase training time, while decreasing the learning rate or epochs would not address slow convergence.

**Learn more:** [Fine-Tune a Model - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-fine-tune.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deployed an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to an endpoint by using the `CreateModel` API operation. The network created by the API call includes two private subnets and one security group.  
  
The model must download data from, and upload data to, an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic to the S3 bucket must not traverse the internet.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the security group to allow outbound connections. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the NAT gateway.
Create a gateway VPC endpoint. Configure an endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.
Create an interface VPC endpoint. Verify that the security group allows only inbound connections. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.
Create a Gateway Load Balancer VPC endpoint. Configure an IAM policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint provides private connectivity from resources in VPC private subnets to S3 without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device. Associating the endpoint with the applicable route tables routes S3-destined traffic through the endpoint, and an endpoint policy can restrict permitted access to the specified S3 bucket.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.domain: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A manufacturing company uses an ML model to decide whether products satisfy a quality standard. The model outputs either **"Passed"** or **"Failed."** Robots use the model to analyze assembly-line photos and sort products into the two categories.  
  
Which metrics should the company use to assess the model's performance? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Precision and recall
Root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)
Accuracy and F1 score
Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score
Perplexity

questions.explanation:
A Passed/Failed quality decision is a binary classification task. Precision and recall quantify false-positive and false-negative performance, respectively; accuracy measures the proportion of correct classifications; and F1 combines precision and recall into one balanced classification metric. Microsoft Learn lists accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 among classification-model evaluation metrics.

**Learn more:** [Evaluate Model: Component Reference — Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/component-reference/evaluate-model?view=azureml-api-2) · [ML.NET metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/machine-learning/resources/metrics)

questions.domain: ML Model Development

options.text: Increase the learning rate and decrease the mini-batch size.
Increase the learning rate as the number of epochs increases.
Decrease the learning rate and increase the mini-batch size.
Decrease the learning rate and decrease the mini-batch size.

questions.explanation:
A lower learning rate reduces the size of parameter updates, helping prevent overshooting and unstable convergence. A larger mini-batch produces a less noisy gradient estimate, which stabilizes updates and validation performance. AWS documentation notes that high learning rates can overshoot and become unstable, while mini-batch size controls gradient-estimation noise.

**Learn more:** [Hyperparameters for optimizing the learning process of your text generation models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-llms-finetuning-hyperparameters.html) · [Distributed training optimization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/distributed-training-optimize.html)

questions.question:
A company has historical data indicating whether customers required long-term support from company staff. The company must develop an ML model to predict whether new customers will require long-term support.  
  
Which modeling approach should the company use to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Anomaly detection
Linear regression
Logistic regression
Semantic segmentation

questions.explanation:

Logistic regression is a supervised learning method for binary classification and can estimate the probability of the support-required class. questions.question:
A company has historical data indicating whether customers required long-term support from company staff. The company must develop an ML model to predict whether new customers will require long-term support.  
  
Which modeling approach should the company use to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use Snappy to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
Use XZ to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
Use XZ to convert the files to Apache Parquet format and to compress the files.
Use gzip to convert the files to Apache Parquet and to compress the files.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker DeepAR accepts JSON Lines or Apache Parquet training data, and Apache Parquet files can be compressed with gzip. DeepAR can process multiple input files from a directory, making gzip-compressed Parquet appropriate for the time-series files.

**Learn more:** [Use the SageMaker AI DeepAR forecasting algorithm](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deepar.html) · [Parameters for Built-in Algorithms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/common-info-all-im-models.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use Amazon Bedrock-supported large language models (LLMs) to build a chat interface for its internal technical documentation. The company stores the documentation in dozens of text files totaling several megabytes. The company updates the text files frequently.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner?

options.text: Create a new LLM on Amazon Bedrock. Train the new LLM on the original dataset and the company documentation. Make the new model available in Bedrock for calls from the chat interface.
Integrate the company documentation with Amazon Bedrock guardrails. Invoke the guardrails for all Amazon Bedrock calls from the chat interface.
Use all the text files to fine tune a model in Amazon Bedrock. Use the fine-tuned model to process user prompts.
Upload all the text files to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Use the knowledge base to provide context when the chat interface makes calls to Amazon Bedrock.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to retrieve relevant proprietary documents and supply them as context to the model at inference time, avoiding continual model training or fine-tuning. Data-source synchronization is incremental, so only documents added, changed, or deleted since the previous sync are processed—well suited to frequently updated documentation.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-how-it-works.html) · [Modify a data source for your Amazon Bedrock knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-ds-update.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is configuring an Amazon SageMaker AI pipeline for an ML model. The pipeline must automatically start a retraining job whenever any data drift is detected.  
  
How should the ML engineer configure the pipeline to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use an AWS Glue crawler and an AWS Glue extract, transform and load (ETL) job to detect data drift. Use AWS Glue triggers to automate the re-training job.
Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to detect data drift. Use an AWS Lambda function to automate the re-training job.
Use SageMaker Model Monitor to detect data drift. Use an AWS Lambda function to automate the re-training job.
Use Amazon QuickSight anomaly detection to detect data drift. Use an AWS Step Functions workflow to automate the re-training job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor detects data drift through data-quality monitoring rules and alerts on violations. An AWS Lambda function can respond to the alert or event and initiate the retraining job automatically.

**Learn more:** [Data quality - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html) · [SageMaker Model Monitor - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-mlops.html)

A company uses Amazon EMR. It has a large Amazon S3 dataset that must be ingested into Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. The dataset includes historical data and real-time streaming data.  
  
The company must ensure that the Feature Store online store receives the latest data as soon as it is available. It must also retain a complete Feature Store offline store for batch processing.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the PutRecord API in Feature Store Runtime to ingest all the data into the online store.
Use the PutRecord API in Feature Store Runtime to ingest all the data into the offline store.
Use the Feature Store Spark connector to ingest the data as Spark DataFrames with the online store and offline store enabled.
Use the Feature Store Spark connector to ingest the data as Spark DataFrames with only the online store enabled.

questions.explanation:
The Feature Store Spark connector supports ingestion of Spark DataFrames from Amazon EMR when both the online and offline stores are enabled. It updates the online store through `PutRecord`, where the record with the greatest event time is retained, and it ingests the data into the offline store to preserve historical data for batch processing. This supports large-scale historical ingestion while maintaining the latest online feature values.

**Learn more:** [Batch ingestion with Amazon SageMaker Feature Store Spark](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-ingestion-spark-connector-setup.html) · [Data sources and ingestion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store-ingest-data.html)

An ML engineer needs an Amazon SageMaker notebook to stop automatically after it has been idle for 1 hour.  
  
How can the ML engineer achieve this?

options.text: Create a lifecycle configuration in SageMaker. Copy the auto-stop-idle script from GitHub to the Start Notebook section.
Create a lifecycle configuration in SageMaker. Copy the auto-stop-idle script from GitHub to the Create Notebook section.
Track the notebook's CPU metric by using Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from CloudWatch Logs to shut down the notebook instance if CPU utilization becomes zero.
Track the notebook's memory metric by using Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from CloudWatch Logs to shut down the notebook instance if memory utilization becomes zero.

questions.explanation:
A SageMaker notebook instance lifecycle configuration can install the auto-stop-idle script through the Start Notebook (OnStart) hook. OnStart runs each time the notebook instance starts, including its initial creation, so the idle-monitoring process is configured after every restart. The Create Notebook (OnCreate) hook runs only once.

**Learn more:** [Create a lifecycle configuration script - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/notebook-lifecycle-config-create.html) · [CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig - Amazon SageMaker API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an AI-assistant research application that uses an Amazon Kendra GenAI Enterprise Edition index. The application will allow users to query documents stored in a Confluence (Cloud) software as a service (SaaS) application. The application will return context-aware, summarized responses. The company must ensure that only the application can query the Amazon Kendra GenAI Enterprise Edition index.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a data source by using the Amazon Kendra Confluence connector V2.0. Configure OAuth 2.0 credentials by using AWS Secrets Manager.
Encrypt the AWS Secrets Manager credentials with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that allows kms:Decrypt permissions for the application IAM role.

Use the third-party CDATA custom Java Database Connectivity AWS Glue connector for Confluence. Associate an AWS Secrets Manager secret configured with Confluence cloud OAuth 2.0 credentials with the AWS Glue connector.
Enable zero-ETL integration with the AWS Glue data source. Configure the target with kms:Decrypt permissions for the application IAM role.
Configure the Amazon Kendra index IAM role with read access to the AWS Glue data source. Configure the application IAM role with kms:Decrypt permissions.

questions.explanation:
To index Confluence Cloud content, you use the native Amazon Kendra Confluence connector V2.0 and store the Confluence OAuth 2.0 credentials in AWS Secrets Manager (A), which is the supported, lowest-overhead ingestion path. Because Kendra's IAM role must be able to get and decrypt that secret, encrypting the Secrets Manager secret with a KMS key whose policy grants kms:Decrypt to the application/connector IAM role (B) enforces that only the intended principal can access the credentials and drive the index. Option C uses an unnecessary third-party CDATA Glue connector, and Options D and E invent a Glue "zero-ETL" data source path that does not apply to the direct Confluence connector scenario.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Kendra Confluence connector V2.0](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kendra/latest/dg/data-source-v2-confluence.html) · [Index Confluence content with Confluence connector V2](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/index-your-confluence-content-using-the-new-confluence-connector-v2-for-amazon-kendra/)

A company needs to install a custom script on all newly created Amazon SageMaker notebook instances.  
  
Which solution satisfies this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a lifecycle configuration script to install the custom script when a new SageMaker notebook is created. Attach the lifecycle configuration to every new SageMaker notebook as part of the creation steps.

Create a custom Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) image that contains the custom script. Push the ECR image to a Docker registry. Attach the Docker image to a SageMaker Studio domain. Select the kernel to run as part of the SageMaker notebook.

Create a custom package index repository. Use AWS CodeArtifact to manage the installation of the custom script. Set up AWS PrivateLink endpoints to connect CodeArtifact to the SageMaker instance. Install the script.

Store the custom script in Amazon S3. Create an AWS Lambda function to install the custom script on new SageMaker notebooks. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function when a new SageMaker notebook is initialized.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon SageMaker notebook instance lifecycle configuration can include an `OnCreate` shell script that runs once when the notebook instance is created. This provides native, automatic installation at provisioning time with minimal supporting infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig.html) · [Create a lifecycle configuration script for a SageMaker notebook instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/notebook-lifecycle-config-create.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to build a credit-risk assessment model. During model validation, the company observes that the model reaches 82% accuracy on validation data but achieved 99% accuracy on training data. The company must resolve the model-accuracy issue before deployment.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Add more dense layers to increase model complexity. Implement batch normalization. Use early stopping during training.
Implement dropout layers. Use L1 or L2 regularization. Perform k-fold cross-validation.
Use principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce the feature dimensionality. Decrease model layers. Implement cross-entropy loss functions.
Augment the training dataset. Remove duplicate records from the training dataset. Implement stratified sampling.

questions.explanation:
A substantially higher training accuracy than validation accuracy is evidence of overfitting. Dropout and L1 or L2 regularization reduce overfitting by limiting reliance on individual neurons and overly large model weights. K-fold cross-validation evaluates performance across multiple training and validation splits, helping assess generalization and reduce overfitting-related selection bias.

**Learn more:** [Example: Viewing a Training and Validation Curve - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-valid-curve.html) · [Metrics and validation - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-metrics-validation.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to develop an ML model using tabular data from its customers. The data includes meaningful ordered features containing sensitive information that must not be discarded. Before another team begins building the model, an ML engineer must ensure the sensitive data is masked.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Made to categorize the sensitive data.
Prepare the data by using AWS Glue DataBrew.
Run an AWS Batch job to change the sensitive data to random values.
Run an Amazon EMR job to change the sensitive data to random values.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew is a managed visual data-preparation service for tabular datasets and provides PII masking mechanisms, including substitution, shuffling, encryption, masking, and hashing. It can therefore obfuscate sensitive values before model development while preserving the data for downstream use.

**Learn more:** [Identifying and handling personally identifiable information (PII) in AWS Glue DataBrew](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/personal-information-protection.html) · [AWS Glue DataBrew recipe step and function reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/recipe-actions-reference.html)

After training the model, the ML engineer deploys it for inference by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The ML engineer wants to monitor the model predictions to identify whether the production data distribution differs from the training data distribution when customer behaviors change.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

An ML engineer plans to use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to preprocess a dataset. The ML engineer intends to use the processed dataset to train a classification model. During preprocessing, the ML engineer observes that a text feature has thousands of values that vary only because of spelling mistakes. The ML engineer must apply an encoding method so that, once preprocessing is complete, the text feature can be used to train the model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Perform ordinal encoding to represent categories of the feature.
Perform similarity encoding to represent categories of the feature.
Perform one-hot encoding to represent categories of the feature.
Perform target encoding to represent categories of the feature.

questions.explanation:
Similarity encoding is intended for categorical columns with a large number of values and noisy data. It creates embeddings in which similar strings receive similar vector representations, so values that differ only by spelling errors can be represented appropriately for model training.

**Learn more:** [Transform Data - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer configures auto scaling for an inference component of a model running behind an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. The ML engineer sets up SageMaker AI auto scaling with a target tracking scaling policy of 100 invocations per model per minute. The SageMaker AI endpoint scales correctly during normal business hours. However, the ML engineer observes that, at the beginning of every business day, zero instances are available to serve requests, causing processing delays.  
  
The ML engineer must make sure that the SageMaker AI endpoint can process incoming requests at the beginning of each business day.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Reduce the SageMaker AI auto scaling cooldown period to the minimum supported value. Add an auto scaling lifecycle hook to scale the SageMaker AI instances.
Change the target metric to CPU utilization.
Modify the scaling policy target value to one.

Apply a step scaling policy that scales based on an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Apply a second CloudWatch alarm and scaling policy to scale the minimum number of instances from zero to one at the start of each business day.

questions.explanation:
A target tracking policy using invocations per model cannot proactively restore capacity after the endpoint has scaled to zero, because no active model copies are available to emit the per-copy invocation metric. SageMaker AI requires a step scaling policy associated with an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale an inference component out from zero. A separate time-based alarm and scaling action that raises the minimum capacity from zero to one at the start of the business day provides ready capacity before requests arrive.

**Learn more:** [Scale an endpoint to zero instances - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-zero-instances.html) · [Auto scaling policy overview - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-policy.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an ML model to classify motion in videos. The data is stored in MP4 format in Amazon S3. When the company created the model, it required 4 months to label every video frame.  
  
The company must retrain the model by using an existing training workflow in Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution that reduces the labeling time.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Ground Truth to annotate the video frames.
Use SageMaker JumpStart to use pre-trained computer vision models to develop a labeling model.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to create a data workflow. Use the workflow to optimize the labeling process.
Use the labeling interface of Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) with Amazon Rekognition to label the video frames.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth supports built-in video-frame labeling jobs and can automatically extract frames from MP4 video files. Its video object detection and object tracking workflows provide specialized annotation tools and worker interfaces for labeling video frames, reducing the effort required to prepare retraining data. [Videos and video frame labeling — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-video.html)

**Learn more:** [Videos and video frame labeling — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-video.html) · [Video frames — Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-video-task-types.html)

options.text: Configure the application to invoke an AWS Lambda function that runs a SageMaker Clarify job.

Use AWS Glue Data Quality to monitor bias.

questions.question:
An ML engineer is assessing several ML models and must select one for production use. The cost of the models’ false-negative predictions is much greater than the cost of their false-positive predictions.  
  
Which metric result should the ML engineer prioritize **MOST** when selecting the model?

options.text: Low precision
High precision
Low recall
High recall

questions.explanation:
High recall indicates that the model identifies a larger share of actual positive cases and therefore produces fewer false negatives. When false negatives carry the greater cost, maximizing recall is the appropriate priority.\
\
**Learn more:** [Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer has an Amazon Comprehend custom model in Account A in the us-east-1 Region. The ML engineer must copy the model to Account В in the same Region.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to make a copy of the model. Transfer the copy to Account B.
Create a resource-based IAM policy. Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation to copy the model to Account B.
Use AWS DataSync to replicate the model from Account A to Account B.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between Account A and Account В to transfer the model.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend can replicate a trained custom model across AWS accounts in the same Region. A resource-based policy on the source model version authorizes Account B to import it, and the `ImportModel` API creates a new, fully trained duplicate in the target account. This avoids copying training data or configuring separate data-transfer or network infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Copying custom models between AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/custom-copy.html) · [Importing a custom model from another AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/custom-copy-importing.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer plans to use a collection of survey responses as training data for an ML classifier. Every survey response is either “yes” or “no.”  
  
The ML engineer must transform the responses into a feature that will improve model-training results, without increasing the dataset’s dimensionality.  
  
Which methods satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Binary encoding
Label encoding
One-hot encoding
Statistical imputation
Tokenization

questions.explanation:
A yes/no field is a binary categorical feature. Binary encoding can represent its two possible values with a single binary digit, and label encoding can map the values to a single numeric feature such as 0 and 1. Both preserve the original feature dimensionality. One-hot encoding creates an indicator feature for each category, so it increases dimensionality.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler: Transform Data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html) · [Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler: Data Insights definitions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-data-insights.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company must store clinical data that contains personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information (PHI).  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution that ensures the PII and PHI are not used to train ML models.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store the clinical data in Amazon S3 buckets. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to mask the PII and PHI before the data is used for model training.
Upload the clinical data to an Amazon Redshift database. Use built-in SQL stored procedures to automatically classify and mask the PII and PHI before the data is used for model training.
Use Amazon Comprehend to detect and mask the PII before the data is used for model training. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and mask the PHI before the data is used for model training.
Create an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the PII and PHI. Program the Lambda function to save the encrypted data to an Amazon S3 bucket for model training.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Comprehend can identify and redact PII in text, and Amazon Comprehend Medical can detect PHI entities in clinical text. Masking the detected sensitive entities before supplying the data to training prevents PII and PHI from being included in ML model training data.

**Learn more:** [Detecting PII entities - Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/how-pii.html) · [Detect PHI - Amazon Comprehend Medical](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend-medical/latest/dev/textanalysis-phi.html)

A company’s ML engineer is developing a classification model. While examining the dataset, the engineer finds a column named `day_of_week`. Its data includes the following values: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.  
  
Which technique should the ML engineer use to convert the data in this column into binary values?

options.text: Binary encoding
Label encoding
One-hot encoding
Tokenization

questions.explanation:
One-hot encoding converts each distinct day-of-week category into a binary indicator feature. This preserves the categories without implying that one day has a greater numeric value or rank than another.\
\
**Learn more:** [SageMaker Data Wrangler: Transform Data (one-hot encoding)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-transform.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows

options.text: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the data. Use Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to mount the S3 bucket to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the data. Mount the file system to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to store the data. Mount the file system to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to store the data. Mount the volume to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS provides a managed NFS file system that Linux clients can mount from AWS and from on-premises servers connected to the VPC by AWS Direct Connect or a Site-to-Site VPN. EFS supports NFS version 4 file locking, including byte-range locking, which satisfies the data-producer locking requirement. Mountpoint for Amazon S3 does not support file locking, and Amazon EBS is block storage rather than a shared NFS file system.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Features of Amazon EFS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/features.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is conducting A/B testing on a model that provides product recommendations. The company has deployed two versions of the model and is randomly displaying each model version to 50% of users.  
  
Which metric should the company use to assess whether users act on a recommendation?

options.text: The conversion rates between the two versions of the model
The number of recommendations provided to each user
The model accuracy on held-out test data
The latency of model inference

questions.explanation:
Conversion rate measures the proportion of users who complete the desired action after receiving a recommendation. Comparing conversion rates across the randomly assigned model versions directly evaluates the recommendations’ effect on user actions; it is an online business-outcome metric rather than an offline model-quality or operational metric.

**Learn more:** [Measuring recommendation impact with A/B testing — Amazon Personalize](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/personalize/latest/dg/ab-testing-recommendations.html) · [Observability — Amazon EKS Best Practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/aiml-observability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer is examining a classification dataset before training a model in Amazon SageMarker AI. The ML engineer suspects the dataset has a significant imbalance among class labels that could result in biased model predictions. To verify class imbalance, the ML engineer must choose an appropriate pre-training bias metric.  
  
Which metric meets this requirement?

options.text: Mean square error (MSE)
Difference in proportions of labels (DPL)
Silhouette score
Structural similarity index measure (SSIM)

questions.explanation:
Difference in proportions of labels (DPL) is a pre-training bias metric that compares the proportions of observed positive labels across facets. A large absolute DPL indicates unequal label outcomes in the training data, which a model can reproduce as biased predictions.

**Learn more:** [Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-data-bias-metric-true-label-imbalance.html) · [Pre-training Bias Metrics - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-measure-data-bias.html)

questions.question:
A company maintains a large, unstructured dataset that contains many duplicate records across several key attributes.  
  
Which AWS solution will identify duplicates in the dataset with the **LEAST** code development?

options.text: Use Amazon Mechanical Turk jobs to detect duplicates.
Use Amazon QuickSight ML Insights to build a custom deduplication model.
Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to pre-process and detect duplicates.
Use the AWS Glue FindMatches transform to detect duplicates.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue FindMatches is a managed machine learning transform for identifying duplicate or matching records, including records without a shared unique identifier or exact field matches. It is designed for record deduplication and can be configured through AWS Glue with minimal custom code.\
\
**Learn more:** [Record matching with AWS Lake Formation FindMatches](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/machine-learning.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
A company intends to deploy an ML model for production inference on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The average inference payload size will range from 100 MB to 300 MB. Inference requests must be completed within 60 minutes or less.  
  
Which SageMaker inference option satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Serverless inference
Asynchronous inference
Real-time inference
Batch transform

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference is designed for endpoint requests with payloads up to 1 GB and processing times of up to one hour. It therefore supports 100–300 MB inference payloads that must finish within 60 minutes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Inference options in Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model-options.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
A company intends to deploy an ML model for production inference on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The average inference payload size will range from 100 MB to 300 MB. Inference requests must be completed within 60 minutes or less.  
  
Which SageMaker inference option satisfies these requirements?

options.text: The AWS Glue service quotas have been reached.
The network bandwidth between the IoT devices and the AWS Region is insufficient.
The AWS Glue ETL jobs are not optimized for parallel processing.
The AWS Glue execution role is missing Amazon S3 permissions.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue enforces service quotas, including quotas for concurrent job runs and concurrent compute capacity. Reaching one of these limits causes Glue job-run throttling or concurrency errors, which delays processing and can create a backlog that makes the overall ingestion pipeline appear slower. AWS documents that an error is returned when a job’s concurrency threshold is reached, and that the maximum is controlled by a service limit.

**Learn more:** [Configuring job properties for Spark jobs in AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-job.html) · [AWS Glue endpoints and quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/glue.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is training a deep learning model to identify abnormalities in images. It has limited GPU resources and a large hyperparameter space to explore. The company must evaluate different configurations while avoiding wasted compute time on poorly performing models that exhibit weak validation accuracy in early epochs.  
  
Which hyperparameter optimization strategy should the company use?

options.text: Grid search across all possible combinations
Bayesian optimization with early stopping
Manual tuning of each parameter individually
Exhaustive search without early stopping

questions.explanation:
Bayesian optimization chooses subsequent hyperparameter trials using the performance of prior trials, making it more sample-efficient than exhaustive grid search for a large search space. Early stopping ends trials with persistently weak early validation accuracy, conserving limited GPU capacity. Azure Machine Learning documents Bayesian sampling as selecting new samples from prior results to improve the primary metric efficiently and documents early-termination policies for ending low-performing jobs.

**Learn more:** [Hyperparameter tuning a model (v2) - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-tune-hyperparameters?view=azureml-api-2)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer must deploy a trained model based on a genetic algorithm. The algorithm solves a complex problem and may require several minutes to produce predictions.  
  
After deployment, the model must access large volumes of data to process requests. Requests can contain up to 100 MB of data.  
  
Which deployment solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy the model to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint.
Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint.
Package the model as a container. Deploy the model to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference is intended for queued inference requests with large payloads—up to 1 GB—and long processing times—up to one hour. It provides managed endpoint hosting and asynchronous processing, meeting the 100 MB and several-minute requirements without managing the underlying EC2, load-balancing, or container infrastructure. SageMaker real-time inference is designed for much smaller, shorter synchronous requests.

**Learn more:** [Asynchronous inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/async-inference.html) · [Model Hosting FAQs - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/hosting-faqs.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must ingest data from Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Snowflake into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. The imported data must always reflect the latest changes in the source systems.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use direct connections to import data from the data sources into Data Wrangler.
Use cataloged connections to import data from the data sources into Data Wrangler.
Use AWS Glue to extract data from the data sources. Use AWS Glue also to import the data directly into Data Wrangler.
Use AWS Lambda to extract data from the data sources. Use Lambda also to import the data directly into Data Wrangler.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler direct connections always access the most recent data in the source system, so updated Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, or Snowflake data can be imported without relying on a prior data transfer. Cataloged connections are transfer results and might not contain the latest source updates.

**Learn more:** [Import data with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler-import.html)

questions.domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has substantially increased the volume of data stored as `.csv` files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Data-transformation scripts and queries now take much longer to run than they did previously.  
  
An ML engineer must implement a solution that optimizes the data for query performance.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure an AWS Lambda function to split the .csv files into smaller objects in the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Glue job to drop columns that have string type values and to save the results to the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Apache Parquet format.
Configure an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data that is in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Apache Parquet is a compressed columnar format that reduces the amount of data analytical queries need to read by loading only needed columns and allowing query engines to skip irrelevant data blocks. An AWS Glue ETL job provides a managed, serverless way to convert the CSV data to Parquet, avoiding the cluster management required by Amazon EMR. AWS documents AWS Glue ETL as an option for converting CSV data to columnar formats and identifies Parquet as beneficial for query performance.

**Learn more:** [Use columnar storage formats - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/columnar-storage.html) · [Optimize data - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/performance-tuning-data-optimization-techniques.html)

questions.domain: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must host a custom ML model for forecast analysis. The forecast analysis will run under a predictable, sustained load during the same 2-hour window each day.  
  
Multiple invocations during the analysis window require fast responses. The company needs AWS to manage the underlying infrastructure and all auto scaling activities.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Schedule an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job by using AWS Lambda.
Configure an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to use scheduled scaling.
Use Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference with provisioned concurrency.
Run the model on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2 with pod auto scaling.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference removes the need to manage serving infrastructure and automatically handles scaling. Provisioned concurrency keeps the allocated endpoint capacity initialized and warm, providing predictable, millisecond-scale response readiness for the repeated low-latency invocations in the known daily analysis window.

**Learn more:** [Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html) · [Automatically scale Provisioned Concurrency for a serverless endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints-autoscale.html)

A company uses an ML model to recommend videos to its users. The model is deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI. Although the model performed well immediately after deployment, its performance has degraded over time.  
  
Which solution can the company use to detect model drift in the future?

options.text: Create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Then create a baseline from the training dataset.
Create a baseline from the training dataset. Then create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor.
Create a baseline by using a built-in rule in SageMaker Clarify. Monitor the drift in Amazon CloudWatch.
Retrain the model on new data. Compare the retrained model's performance to the original model’s performance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor establishes baseline statistics and constraints from a reference dataset, typically the training dataset, and a monitoring schedule compares later captured data and model results against that baseline to identify drift or violations. The baseline must exist before the monitoring job is created.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Schedule data quality monitoring jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-schedule-data-monitor.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a conversational AI assistant that routes requests through Amazon Bedrock to an Anthropic Claude large language model (LLM). Users report that, when they ask similar questions repeatedly, they occasionally get different answers. An ML engineer must make the responses more consistent and less random.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Increase the temperature parameter and the top_k parameter.
Increase the temperature parameter. Decrease the top_k parameter.
Decrease the temperature parameter. Increase the top_k parameter.
Decrease the temperature parameter and the top_k parameter.

questions.explanation:
A lower temperature favors higher-probability token choices and produces more deterministic output. A lower `top_k` restricts each next-token selection to fewer of the most likely candidates, excluding lower-probability alternatives. Decreasing both reduces variability in Anthropic Claude responses on Amazon Bedrock.

**Learn more:** [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html) · [Request and Response - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-request-response.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A travel company wants to build an ML model that recommends each user’s next airport destination. The company has collected millions of records containing user location, recent search history on the company website, and 2,000 available airports. The data includes several categorical features with a target column expected to have a high-dimensional sparse matrix.  
  
The company must use Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithms for the model. An ML engineer transforms the categorical features by using one-hot encoding.  
  
Which algorithm should the ML engineer implement to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use the CatBoost algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
Use the DeepAR forecasting algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
Use the Factorization Machines algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
Use the k-means algorithm to cluster users into groups. Map each group to the next airport destination based on user search history.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI Factorization Machines is designed to capture pairwise feature interactions efficiently in high-dimensional sparse datasets and is explicitly suited to item-recommendation use cases. One-hot encoding categorical location, search-history, and airport values produces precisely this sparse feature representation.

**Learn more:** [Factorization Machines Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/fact-machines.html)

questions.domain: ML Model Development
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ML engineer used min-max normalization in AWS Glue DataBrew to normalize training data. Before sending production inference data to the model for predictions, the ML engineer must normalize it in the same manner as the training data.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Apply statistics from a well-known dataset to normalize the production samples.
Keep the min-max normalization statistics from the training set. Use these values to normalize the production samples.
Calculate a new set of min-max normalization statistics from a batch of production samples. Use these values to normalize all the production samples.
Calculate a new set of min-max normalization statistics from each production sample. Use these values to normalize all the production samples.

questions.explanation:
Min-max scaling depends on the minimum and maximum values used to fit the transformation. Reusing the training set’s statistics applies the identical feature mapping at inference time and prevents training-serving skew. AWS Glue DataBrew’s `MIN_MAX` normalization rescales numeric values to the range `[0,1]`.

**Learn more:** [AWS Glue DataBrew Developer Guide — Data science recipe steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/recipe-actions.data-science.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company develops a recommendation model and hosts it on an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. The model uses the SageMaker AI endpoint for near real-time inference to provide customers with personalized product recommendations based on browsing history, purchase records, and in-app user interactions.  
  
Following a major marketing campaign, the company notices a sharp decline in model performance. The company needs a solution that can proactively monitor, detect, and validate model performance before future marketing campaigns.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Clarify to analyze changes in feature distribution. Configure SageMaker Model Monitor for near real-time input validation.
Use Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to monitor endpoint metrics. Use SageMaker Model Monitor to track feature attribution.
Use SageMaker Clarify for bias detection. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor model latency.
Use SageMaker Model Monitor to monitor constraints. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to analyze error patterns.

questions.explanation:
SageMaker Model Monitor compares captured real-time endpoint inputs with baseline statistics and constraints, identifying violations caused by data-quality or distribution drift. SageMaker Clarify monitors feature-attribution drift, revealing changes in how input features affect recommendation predictions. Together, these capabilities detect data changes and validate changing model behavior before performance degradation affects a campaign.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Feature attribution drift for models in production](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-monitor-feature-attribution-drift.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an Amazon S3 bucket to gather data that will support ML workflows. The company must use AWS Glue DataBrew to clean and normalize this data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a DataBrew dataset by using the S3 path. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew profile job.
Create a DataBrew dataset by using the S3 path. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew recipe job.
Create a DataBrew dataset by using a Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver to connect to the S3 bucket. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew profile job.
Create a DataBrew dataset by using a Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver to connect to the S3 bucket. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew recipe job.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew recipe jobs apply transformation steps from a DataBrew recipe to a dataset, including cleaning and normalization, and can use data sourced from Amazon S3. Profile jobs instead analyze a dataset to generate statistics and a data profile; they do not transform it. JDBC is not the connection method for an Amazon S3 bucket.

**Learn more:** [Creating and working with AWS Glue DataBrew recipe jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/jobs.recipe.html) · [Creating, running, and scheduling AWS Glue DataBrew jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/databrew/latest/dg/jobs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an ML project that will use Amazon SageMaker notebook instances. An ML engineer must ensure the SageMaker notebook instances do not permit root access.  
  
Which solution will prevent deployment of notebook instances that permit root access?

options.text: Use IAM condition keys to stop deployments of SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stop deployments of SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
Monitor resource creation by using Amazon EventBridge events. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes all deployed SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
Monitor resource creation by using AWS CloudFormation events. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes all deployed SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.

questions.explanation:
An IAM policy can use the `sagemaker:RootAccess` condition key to deny `CreateNotebookInstance` and `UpdateNotebookInstance` requests when root access is set to `Enabled`. This enforces the requirement before a notebook instance is created or updated. SageMaker notebook instances default to root access unless the `RootAccess` setting is disabled.

**Learn more:** [Actions, resources, and condition keys for Amazon SageMaker](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonsagemaker.html) · [Control root access to a SageMaker notebook instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/nbi-root-access.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an ML model deployed to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time inference. The company must deploy a new model and compare its performance with that of the currently deployed model before moving all traffic to the new model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Deploy the new model to a separate endpoint. Manually split traffic between the two endpoints.
Deploy the new model to a separate endpoint. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute traffic between the two endpoints.
Deploy the new model as a shadow variant on the same endpoint as the current model. Route a portion of live traffic to the shadow model for evaluation.
Use AWS Lambda functions with custom logic to route traffic between the current model and the new model.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker shadow variants can run a new model alongside the current production variant on the same endpoint. SageMaker replicates a configurable portion of live requests to the shadow variant, compares operational metrics such as latency and error rate, and allows the shadow variant to be promoted after validation without building separate routing infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Shadow tests - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests.html) · [Create a shadow test - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests-create.html)
